### Summary: Machine Learning E-Commerce Repurchase Customer Prediction Model

Recent advances in machine learning have led to the development of robust, multi-faceted models capable of accurately predicting customer repurchase behavior on e-commerce platforms. These models leverage a combination of supervised and unsupervised techniques, ensemble learning strategies, and deep learning architectures to capture complex, non-linear patterns in large-scale, heterogeneous customer data.

#### Key Methods and Features

1. **Hybrid and Ensemble Models**
   - Hybrid models combining algorithms such as XGBoost with logistic regression or k-means clustering with support vector machines consistently outperform single algorithm models in repurchase prediction tasks. These hybrids address overfitting, exploit complementary strengths, and improve generalization (e.g., stacking with meta-learners like XGBoost).
   - Feature engineering approaches like feature selection (e.g., SSP algorithm) and SMOTE-based class balancing significantly improve model accuracy by reducing complexity and mitigating class imbalances.

2. **Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering**
   - Extensive preprocessing—handling missing values, normalization, one-hot encoding, text mining (e.g., with NLP, BERT, or TF-IDF for reviews), and sentiment analysis—is critical to transform raw e-commerce data into actionable features.
   - Behavioral (e.g., session frequency, purchase recency), demographic, financial (cashback, spending), and psychographic signals are all integrated to form comprehensive feature sets.
   - Spatial and temporal features such as browsing patterns, days since last purchase, and seasonal indicators are also leveraged to capture dynamic customer behavior.

3. **Segmentation and Personalization**
   - Customer segmentation via clustering (e.g., K-Means, RFM-based) enhances model interpretability and identifies high-value, at-risk, or churn-prone segments, enabling targeted retention strategies.
   - Personalization is facilitated by integrating user IDs, session data, and interaction histories, allowing models to focus on relevant behaviors and tailor predictions.

4. **Interpretable and Scalable Approaches**
   - Model interpretability frameworks (e.g., SHAP, LIME) are increasingly applied to explain the drivers of repurchase decisions (e.g., loyalty, support satisfaction, product preference), supporting actionable business insights.
   - Streaming and online learning pipelines (e.g., DBSTREAM) enable real-time or incremental model updates, adapting to changing customer behavior without full retraining.
   - Deep learning architectures, such as CNNs for pattern extraction from product images and LSTMs/RNNs for sequential behavior modeling, augment traditional machine learning methods with advanced contextual understanding.

5. **Performance and Impact**
   - Ensemble methods (e.g., XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest) consistently show superior accuracy, F1-score, precision, recall, and AUC compared to individual models or baseline methods.
   - Predictive power is further enhanced by combining machine learning with dynamic pricing, marketing strategy optimization, and customer lifetime value (CLV) forecasting, all of which benefit from improved repurchase predictions.

Machine learning-based e-commerce repurchase prediction aims to identify customers who are likely to make future purchases by analyzing their transaction history, browsing activity, engagement patterns, demographic characteristics, and customer-value indicators. A prominent approach is the combination of XGBoost and Logistic Regression. Logistic Regression provides a relatively simple and interpretable representation of linear relationships, whereas XGBoost captures more complex and nonlinear interactions among customer characteristics. Fusion of the two models can therefore exploit complementary strengths while reducing weaknesses such as insufficient nonlinear modeling in Logistic Regression and potential overfitting in tree-based models. Balanced positive and negative samples further improve the robustness of XGBoost-based repurchase models, particularly when repeat purchasers constitute an imbalanced class.

Feature engineering and feature selection are equally important. Customer repurchase behavior can be characterized using variables such as recency, purchase frequency, monetary value, tenure, order history, browsing depth, session counts, app activity, time spent on the website, product interactions, discounts, complaints, satisfaction, and engagement metrics. Feature-selection methods such as SSP can reduce redundant or irrelevant variables, simplify model complexity, and improve classification accuracy. Behavioral signals such as browsing, clicking, session activity, and interaction frequency are particularly useful because they capture purchase intent beyond static demographic or explicit-feedback information.

Customer segmentation provides another layer of predictive improvement. RFM analysis combined with K-Means clustering can separate customers according to recency, frequency, and monetary value, creating groups such as loyal high-value customers, growth-potential customers, disengaged customers, and premium spenders. Finer segmentation tends to work especially well for high-frequency customers, whose richer behavioral histories support personalized or one-to-one prediction. For low-frequency customers, sparse interaction data can restrict the benefits of highly granular segmentation.

similar_papers.title: Single image super-resolution via Image Quality Assessment-Guided Deep Learning Network
similar_papers.abstract: In recent years, deep learning (DL) networks have been widely used in super-resolution (SR) and exhibit improved performance. In this paper, an image quality assessment (IQA)-guided single image super-resolution (SISR) method is proposed in DL architecture, in order to achieve a nice tradeoff between perceptual quality and distortion measure of the SR result. Unlike existing DL-based SR algorithms, an IQA net is introduced to extract perception features from SR results, calculate corresponding loss fused with original absolute pixel loss, and guide the adjustment of SR net parameters. To solve the problem of heterogeneous datasets used by IQA and SR networks, an interactive training model is established via cascaded network. We also propose a pairwise ranking hinge loss method to overcome the shortcomings of insufficient samples during training process. The performance comparison between our proposed method with recent SISR methods shows that the former achieves a better tradeoff between perceptual quality and distortion measure than the latter. Extensive benchmark experiments and analyses also prove that our method provides a promising and opening architecture for SISR, which is not confined to a specific network model.

claims.text: An image quality assessment-guided single image super-resolution method using deep learning networks is proposed, which integrates an image quality assessment network to guide the adjustment of super-resolution network parameters, achieving a balance between perceptual quality and distortion measures.

An interactive training mechanism via a cascaded network is established, where the image quality assessment network acts as a supervisor in constructing the loss function of the super-resolution network, addressing the issue of heterogeneous datasets used by the two networks.

A pairwise ranking hinge loss method is introduced to dynamically create training labels, overcoming the challenge of insufficient training samples and reducing overfitting during the training process.

The proposed method demonstrates a better tradeoff between perceptual quality and distortion measures compared to recent single image super-resolution methods, as validated through extensive benchmark experiments and analyses.

The architecture of the proposed method is flexible and not confined to a specific network model, allowing the baseline of the super-resolution network to be adjusted according to practical requirements, such as improving performance or enhancing efficiency.

similar_papers.title: A No-Reference Deep Learning Quality Assessment Method for Super-Resolution Images Based on Frequency Maps
similar_papers.abstract: To support the application scenarios where high-resolution (HR) images are urgently needed, various single image super-resolution (SISR) algorithms are developed. However, SISR is an ill-posed inverse problem, which may bring artifacts like texture shift, blur, etc. to the reconstructed images, thus it is necessary to evaluate the quality of super-resolution images (SRIs). Note that most existing image quality assessment (IQA) methods were developed for synthetically distorted images, which may not work for SRIs since their distortions are more diverse and complicated. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a no-reference deep-learning image quality assessment method based on frequency maps because the artifacts caused by SISR algorithms are quite sensitive to frequency information. Specifically, we first obtain the high-frequency map (HM) and low-frequency map (LM) of SRI by using Sobel operator and piecewise smooth image approximation. Then, a two-stream network is employed to extract the quality-aware features of both frequency maps. Finally, the features are regressed into a single quality value using fully connected layers. The experimental results show that our method outperforms all compared IQA models on the selected three super-resolution quality assessment (SRQA) databases.
similar_papers.venue: International Symposium on Circuits and Systems

open_access_pdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04289, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

claims.text: A no-reference deep learning method for super-resolution image quality assessment is developed, utilizing high-frequency and low-frequency maps generated by Sobel operator and piecewise smooth image approximation to address diverse and complex distortions in super-resolution images.

A two-stream deep learning network with ResNet101 as the backbone is designed to independently extract quality-aware features from high-frequency and low-frequency maps, combining features from the first and last layers for improved performance.
The proposed method employs two-stage fully connected layers to regress extracted features into a single quality score, using mean squared error as the loss function.

Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art full-reference and no-reference image quality assessment models on three super-resolution quality assessment databases, including CVIU, QADS, and SRIJ.
Cross-database validation confirms the generalization ability of the proposed method, showing superior performance compared to other no-reference image quality assessment models.

similar_papers.title: Quality assessment of models and deep learning methods for super-resolution image formation
similar_papers.abstract: This article examines evaluation metrics for the results of super-resolution image generation in solving the SISR task. The study comprises two experiments: the implementation of custom network architectures for SRGAN, VDSR, and SRCNN, and fine-tuning of pre-trained SRGAN, VDSR, and SRCNN models. An algorithm for assessing the quality of models and deep learning methods for generating super-resolution images is suggested. The VDSR model performed best in terms of pixel, structural, and perceptual metrics, as well as training time and visual confirmation by a human, highlighting that residual learning is more effective than recursive learning under the conditions of the two conducted experiments. Threshold values for practically acceptable and high-quality results were determined through visual analysis of many generated images and their corresponding quality metrics, including those reported by other researchers.

claims.text: Residual learning in the VDSR model is more effective than recursive learning for single image super-resolution tasks, as demonstrated by superior performance in pixel, structural, and perceptual metrics, as well as training time and visual quality.

Threshold values for practically acceptable and high-quality super-resolution image results were determined through visual analysis and corresponding quality metrics, including PSNR, MSSIM, and LPIPS.

Deep learning methods, such as VDSR, outperform generative models like SRGAN in single image super-resolution tasks based on comprehensive evaluations of quantitative metrics, perceptual indicators, and human visual perception.

An algorithm for training and evaluating super-resolution models using pre-trained weights improves perceptual quality and avoids overfitting, as evidenced by the VDSR model achieving high MSSIM and LPIPS scores.
The DIV2K dataset provides a diverse and labeled set of low- and high-resolution image pairs, enabling effective training and evaluation of single image super-resolution models.

similar_papers.title: Enhanced Deep Residual Networks for Single Image Super-Resolution
similar_papers.abstract: Recent research on super-resolution has progressed with the development of deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN). In particular, residual learning techniques exhibit improved performance. In this paper, we develop an enhanced deep super-resolution network (EDSR) with performance exceeding those of current state-of-the-art SR methods. The significant performance improvement of our model is due to optimization by removing unnecessary modules in conventional residual networks. The performance is further improved by expanding the model size while we stabilize the training procedure. We also propose a new multi-scale deep super-resolution system (MDSR) and training method, which can reconstruct high-resolution images of different upscaling factors in a single model. The proposed methods show superior performance over the state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets and prove its excellence by winning the NTIRE2017 Super-Resolution Challenge[26].
similar_papers.venue: 2017 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)

claims.text: An enhanced deep super-resolution network (EDSR) improves performance over state-of-the-art single image super-resolution methods by optimizing the residual network architecture through the removal of unnecessary modules and stabilizing training with residual scaling.

A multi-scale deep super-resolution system (MDSR) is proposed, which reconstructs high-resolution images for multiple upscaling factors within a single model by sharing parameters across scales and incorporating scale-specific modules.

The removal of batch normalization layers in the residual network architecture reduces GPU memory usage by approximately 40% during training and allows for the construction of larger models with improved performance.
Training high-scale super-resolution models using pre-trained low-scale models accelerates convergence and improves performance by leveraging inter-scale correlations.
Using L1 loss instead of L2 loss for training super-resolution networks results in better convergence and improved performance in terms of PSNR and SSIM metrics.

similar_papers.title: Single Image Super-Resolution with Deep Learning
similar_papers.abstract: Single Image Super-Resolution (SISR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution images from low-resolution images. With the breakthrough of deep learning technology, especially the introduction of the convolutional neural Network (CNN), significant progress has been made in the field of single-image super-resolution. Although single-image super-resolution technology has developed rapidly, there are still several limitations. First, high-performance models are often computationally complex and difficult to apply in real-time. Second, most methods rely on the idealized degradation assumption, which is difficult to adapt to the complex noise and blur of real scenes. Third, the commonly used evaluation metrics are not completely consistent with human eye perception. Fourth, the generalization ability of the model is limited, and the cross-domain application performance is insufficient. This paper systematically reviews the evolution of this technology since the application of deep learning, focusing on five types of representative models. By comparing and analyzing the architecture innovation and performance of various models, this paper summarizes their respective advantages and limitations, and looks forward to the future development direction of higher accuracy, stronger generalization, and better perceptual quality.

claims.text: The introduction of convolutional neural networks, such as the Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Network (SRCNN), marked a significant breakthrough in single-image super-resolution by enabling end-to-end nonlinear mapping and achieving higher reconstruction quality compared to traditional methods.

Residual networks, exemplified by models like Enhanced Deep Residual Network (EDSR), improve single-image super-resolution by addressing deep network training challenges, removing batch normalization layers to preserve image contrast, and achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction accuracy.

Attention mechanisms, as implemented in models like the Residual Channel Attention Network (RCAN), enhance single-image super-resolution by adaptively emphasizing key features, improving both reconstruction accuracy and perceptual quality.

The integration of graph neural networks and attention mechanisms, as seen in the Channel Attention and Spatial Graph Convolutional Network (CASGCN), improves robustness and performance in complex scenes by modeling global pixel relationships and capturing long-range dependencies.

Hybrid architectures combining convolutional neural networks and Transformers, such as the Aggregation Connection Transformer (ACT), achieve superior single-image super-resolution performance by leveraging local detail recovery from CNNs and global dependency modeling from Transformers.

similar_papers.title: Image Super-Resolution Using Deep Convolutional Networks
similar_papers.abstract: We propose a deep learning method for single image super-resolution (SR). Our method directly learns an end-to-end mapping between the low/high-resolution images. The mapping is represented as a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) that takes the low-resolution image as the input and outputs the high-resolution one. We further show that traditional sparse-coding-based SR methods can also be viewed as a deep convolutional network. But unlike traditional methods that handle each component separately, our method jointly optimizes all layers. Our deep CNN has a lightweight structure, yet demonstrates state-of-the-art restoration quality, and achieves fast speed for practical on-line usage. We explore different network structures and parameter settings to achieve trade-offs between performance and speed. Moreover, we extend our network to cope with three color channels simultaneously, and show better overall reconstruction quality.
similar_papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

claims.text: A deep convolutional neural network (CNN) can be used to directly learn an end-to-end mapping between low-resolution and high-resolution images for single image super-resolution, achieving state-of-the-art restoration quality with minimal pre- and post-processing.

The proposed Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Network (SRCNN) demonstrates that traditional sparse-coding-based super-resolution methods can be reformulated as a deep convolutional neural network, with the advantage of jointly optimizing all layers in an end-to-end manner.

The SRCNN model achieves superior super-resolution performance compared to state-of-the-art example-based methods, while maintaining a lightweight structure and fast processing speed suitable for practical online usage.
The SRCNN model can be extended to process three color channels (e.g., RGB or YCbCr) simultaneously, resulting in improved super-resolution performance for color images.

The performance of SRCNN can be further improved by using larger and more diverse training datasets or by increasing the depth and width of the network, though deeper networks may face challenges in training and diminishing returns in performance improvement.

similar_papers.title: A Systematic Survey of Deep Learning-Based Single-Image Super-Resolution
similar_papers.abstract: Single-image super-resolution (SISR) is an important task in image processing, which aims to enhance the resolution of imaging systems. Recently, SISR has made a huge leap and has achieved promising results with the help of deep learning (DL). In this survey, we give an overview of DL-based SISR methods and group them according to their design targets. Specifically, we first introduce the problem definition, research background, and the significance of SISR. Secondly, we introduce some related works, including benchmark datasets, upsampling methods, optimization objectives, and image quality assessment methods. Thirdly, we provide a detailed investigation of SISR and give some domain-specific applications of it. Fourthly, we present the reconstruction results of some classic SISR methods to intuitively know their performance. Finally, we discuss some issues that still exist in SISR and summarize some new trends and future directions. This is an exhaustive survey of SISR, which can help researchers better understand SISR and inspire more exciting research in this field. An investigation project for SISR is provided at https://github.com/CV-JunchengLi/SISR-Survey.

open_access_pdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14335, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

claims.text: Deep learning-based single-image super-resolution methods have significantly advanced image resolution enhancement by transforming low-resolution images into high-resolution ones through end-to-end frameworks that integrate feature extraction, non-linear mapping, and image reconstruction.

Single-image super-resolution is an ill-posed problem where multiple high-resolution images can correspond to the same low-resolution image, and deep learning techniques address this by leveraging efficient network architectures, loss function designs, and large-scale training datasets.

Deep learning-based single-image super-resolution methods can be categorized into simulation-based approaches, real-world applications, and domain-specific applications, with further subdivisions based on design targets such as efficient network design, perceptual quality improvement, and additional information utilization.

Transformer-based architectures have emerged as a powerful approach in single-image super-resolution, offering superior performance in capturing global image context and achieving state-of-the-art results across various datasets.

Future directions in single-image super-resolution include developing lightweight models for edge devices, flexible models for arbitrary scaling, improved loss functions and assessment methods, and integrating super-resolution with high-level computer vision tasks for mutual performance enhancement.

similar_papers.title: Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution Using Feature Grouped Multi-Scale Network
similar_papers.abstract: Abstract. With the rapid development of deep learning technology, remote sensing image super-resolution has made remarkable progress. Remote sensing images usually contain multiple objects with different scales, making it crucial to adopt multi-scale feature extraction methods. However, the existing multi-scale modules introduce a large number of parameters due to performing convolution operations with different kernel sizes on the input feature maps separately. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Grouped Multi-scale Feature Extraction (GMFE) module. By applying grouped convolutions along the depth dimension of the input feature maps, the number of parameters is effectively reduced. On this basis, we design a Feature-grouped Multi-scale Super-Resolution (FMSR) network. We propose an Edge Enhancement (EE) module integrated into the network to sharpen edges and enhance the visual quality of the image. Additionally, we introduce an arbitrary scale upsampling module, enabling a single trained model to perform image super-resolution reconstruction at arbitrary scales. Extensive experiments on the UC Merced and RSSCN7 datasets demonstrate that the proposed FMSR network achieves superior performance in both quantitative metrics and visual quality.
similar_papers.venue: The International Archives of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences

claims.text: The Grouped Multi-scale Feature Extraction (GMFE) and GMFE+ modules, based on grouped convolution, significantly reduce the number of parameters while maintaining multi-scale feature extraction capabilities for remote sensing image super-resolution.

The Feature-grouped Multi-scale Edge Enhancement (FMEE) module, incorporating an Edge Enhancement mechanism, improves the clarity of image edges, particularly in scenarios with edge blurring and heavy noise.

An arbitrary-scale upsampling module enables a single trained model to perform remote sensing image super-resolution reconstruction at arbitrary scales, improving model generalizability and flexibility.

The Feature-grouped Multi-scale Super-Resolution (FMSR) network, which integrates GMFE, FMEE, and a large-kernel attention mechanism, achieves superior performance in both quantitative metrics and visual quality on the UC Merced and RSSCN7 datasets.

The proposed FMSR network demonstrates the ability to perform efficient and high-quality remote sensing image super-resolution with reduced computational complexity and parameter count compared to traditional multi-scale feature extraction methods.

similar_papers.title: Dual Path Attention and Re-parameterization Network for efficient image super-resolution
similar_papers.abstract: Efficient deep learning based methods have achieved significant performance in single image super-resolution. Recent research on efficient super-resolution has mainly focused on reducing the number of parameters and computational complexity through various network designs, enabling models to be better deployed on resource constrained devices. In this work, we propose a novel and effective super-resolution model based on attention mechanism and structural re-parameterization, called Dual Path Attention and Re-parameterization Network DPARN , which uses a hybrid attention mechanisms to balance the running speed and reconstruction quality of the model. Specifically, we utilize grouped convolution to introduce both parameter free and enhanced spatial attention to improve the feature extraction capability of student networks. Meanwhile, we ado-pted a novel lightweight network training strategy that first uses knowledge distillation for initial training, during which structured knowledge from the teacher network is transmitted to the student network. Then, multiple loss functions are combined to fine-tuning the student network, in order to preserve high-frequency details and avoid excessive smoothing caused by pixel loss. Finally, extensive experiments conducted on four benchmark datasets demonstrated the effectiveness and efficiency of proposed DPARN. Our method achieves PSNR SSIM performance comparable to state-of-the-art efficient super-resolution models, with faster inference speed and fewer network parameters.

claims.text: The Dual Path Attention and Re-parameterization Network (DPARN) introduces a dual-path structure combining Enhanced Spatial Attention and Swift Parameter-free Attention to balance inference speed and reconstruction quality in single image super-resolution tasks.
DPARN employs structural re-parameterization and knowledge distillation techniques to optimize lightweight student networks without increasing computational complexity.
A multi-loss fine-tuning strategy combining Charbonnier loss, perceptual loss, and edge loss improves high-frequency detail restoration and enhances the visual quality of super-resolution images.
The use of grouped convolution in DPARN enables the integration of parameter-free and parameterized attention mechanisms, reducing model size while maintaining performance.

Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DPARN achieves comparable PSNR and SSIM performance to state-of-the-art efficient super-resolution models with faster inference speed and fewer network parameters.

similar_papers.title: Multi-prior physics-enhanced neural network enables pixel super-resolution and twin-image-free phase retrieval from single-shot hologram
similar_papers.abstract: Digital in-line holographic microscopy (DIHM) is a widely used interference technique for real-time reconstruction of living cells’ morphological information with large space-bandwidth product and compact setup. However, the need for a larger pixel size of detector to improve imaging photosensitivity, field-of-view, and signal-to-noise ratio often leads to the loss of sub-pixel information and limited pixel resolution. Additionally, the twin-image appearing in the reconstruction severely degrades the quality of the reconstructed image. The deep learning (DL) approach has emerged as a powerful tool for phase retrieval in DIHM, effectively addressing these challenges. However, most DL-based strategies are data-driven or end-to-end net approaches, suffering from excessive data dependency and limited generalization ability. Here-in, a novel multi-prior physics-enhanced neural network with pixel super-resolution (MPPN-PSR) for phase retrieval of DIHM is proposed. It encapsulates the physical model prior, sparsity prior and deep image prior in an untrained deep neural network. The effectiveness and feasibility of MPPN-PSR are demonstrated by comparing it with other traditional and learning-based phase retrieval methods. With the capabilities of pixel super-resolution, twin-image elimination and high-throughput jointly from a single-shot intensity measurement, the proposed DIHM approach is expected to be widely adopted in biomedical workflow and industrial measurement.

claims.text: A multi-prior physics-enhanced neural network (MPPN-PSR) that integrates physical model prior, sparsity prior, and deep image prior within an untrained deep neural network enables pixel super-resolution, twin-image elimination, and noise-insensitive phase retrieval from single-shot digital in-line holographic microscopy (DIHM) holograms without additional hardware modifications.

The MPPN-PSR method achieves a 3-fold increase in pixel resolution and approximately 2-fold improvement in optical resolution compared to traditional pixel super-resolution methods like TwIST-TV-PSR, while maintaining high throughput and large field-of-view in DIHM.

The MPPN-PSR approach demonstrates superior performance in suppressing twin-image artifacts and noise, achieving higher structural similarity index (SSIM), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and lower no-reference perceptual blur metric (NPBM) compared to existing phase retrieval methods.

The MPPN-PSR method enables high-throughput quantitative phase imaging with enhanced resolution and contrast, allowing detailed observation of biological and industrial samples from single-shot low-resolution holograms.

The MPPN-PSR framework is robust to noise, capable of handling sub-pixel information loss and twin-image artifacts, and can be adapted to different imaging conditions by adjusting the parameters of the forward physical model.

similar_papers.title: Advancing 1.5T MR imaging: toward achieving 3T quality through deep learning super-resolution techniques
similar_papers.abstract: Introduction A 3T MRI scanner delivers enhanced image quality and SNR, minimizing artifacts to provide superior high-resolution brain images compared to a 1.5T MRI. Thus, making it vitally important for diagnosing complex neurological conditions. However, its higher cost of acquisition and operation, increased sensitivity to image distortions, greater noise levels, and limited accessibility in many healthcare settings present notable challenges. These factors impact heterogeneity in MRI neuroimaging data on account of the uneven distribution of 1.5T and 3T MRI scanners across healthcare institutions. Methods In our study, we investigated the efficacy of three deep learning-based super-resolution techniques to enhance 1.5T MRI images, aiming to achieve quality analogous to 3T scans. These synthetic and “upgraded” 1.5T images were compared and assessed against their 3T counterparts using a range of image quality assessment metrics. Specifically, we employed metrics such as the Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS), and Intensity Differences in Pixels (IDP) to evaluate the similitude and visual quality of the enhanced images. Results According to our experimental results it has been exhibited that among the three evaluated deep learning-based super-resolution techniques, the Transformer Enhanced Generative Adversarial Network (TCGAN) significantly outperformed the others. To reduce pixel differences, enhance image sharpness, and preserve essential anatomical details TCGAN performed efficaciously. Discussion This approach presents TCGAN offers a cost-effective and widely accessible alternative for generating high-quality images without the need for expensive, high-field MRI scans and leads to inconsistencies and complicate data comparison and harmonization challenges across studies utilizing various scanners.

claims.text: The Transformer-Enhanced Generative Adversarial Network (TCGAN) significantly outperforms other super-resolution techniques, such as SRGAN, ESPCN, Bicubic, and Lanczos interpolation, in enhancing 1.5T MRI images to achieve quality comparable to 3T MRI scans by reducing pixel intensity differences, enhancing image sharpness, and preserving anatomical details.

The Intensity Differences in Pixels (IDP) metric, developed specifically for this study, provides a detailed evaluation of pixel-level intensity variations and demonstrates that TCGAN-generated synthetic 3T images closely align with original 3T images, outperforming other super-resolution methods.

Super-resolution techniques, particularly TCGAN, offer a cost-effective and accessible alternative to high-field MRI scans by harmonizing image quality differences between 1.5T and 3T MRI scans, which can improve data consistency and reduce challenges in longitudinal imaging studies.

Traditional image quality metrics such as SSIM and PSNR fail to capture subtle perceptual differences critical for clinical applications, whereas the IDP metric effectively quantifies these differences, highlighting the advantages of deep learning-based super-resolution methods over interpolation techniques.

The TCGAN model's hybrid architecture, combining transformer and CNN-based U-Net components with attention mechanisms, enables it to capture global and local image features, resulting in superior performance in generating high-quality synthetic 3T MRI images from 1.5T scans.

similar_papers.title: Enhancing Image Quality via Deep Autoencoder Architectures for Single Image Super-Resolution
similar_papers.abstract: Single Image Super-Resolution (SISR) reconstructs high-resolution (HR) images from low-resolution (LR) inputs. Although deep networks achieve strong results, many incur high computational cost and blur fine textures. We present an efficient deep autoencoder for SISR: an encoder extracts compact LR features, and a decoder synthesizes the HR output. To enhance detail recovery, we incorporate skip connections and residual learning within the reconstruction path. Evaluations on the DIV2K dataset show that the proposed model attains high PSNR and SSIM and surpasses several benchmark methods in reconstruction quality. Ablation studies confirm that each enhancement contributes to sharper edges and more consistent texture reproduction across diverse scenes and images. Compared with lightweight architectures such as FSRCNN, our approach uses moderately more parameters and runs slower on CPUs, yet produces clearly improved visual fidelity. These findings indicate that enhanced autoencoder designs are practical for super-resolution, particularly when deployed on GPUs or edge-accelerated hardware.

claims.text: A deep convolutional autoencoder with skip connections and residual learning improves high-resolution image reconstruction in Single Image Super-Resolution tasks by effectively recovering fine textures and edges while maintaining computational efficiency.

The incorporation of skip connections in the autoencoder architecture enables the preservation of spatial details by directly transferring low-level features from the encoder to the decoder, enhancing texture reconstruction and reducing blurring.

The use of a pixel-wise Mean Squared Error loss function in training the autoencoder achieves competitive reconstruction quality in terms of PSNR and SSIM without relying on perceptual or adversarial losses, making it suitable for resource-constrained environments.

The autoencoder-based model demonstrates superior reconstruction quality compared to lightweight architectures like FSRCNN and achieves comparable or better performance than deeper models like VDSR on the DIV2K dataset.

The proposed autoencoder architecture, with approximately 915K parameters, balances high reconstruction quality and computational efficiency, making it suitable for deployment on GPUs or edge-accelerated hardware.

similar_papers.title: Ultra Sharp : Study of Single Image Super Resolution Using Residual Dense Network
similar_papers.abstract: For years, Single Image Super Resolution (SISR) has been an interesting and ill-posed problem in computer vision. The traditional super-resolution (SR) imaging approaches involve interpolation, reconstruction, and learning-based methods. Interpolation methods are fast and uncomplicated to compute, but they are not so accurate and reliable. Reconstruction-based methods are better compared with interpolation methods, but they are time-consuming and the quality degrades as the scaling increases. Even though learning-based methods like Markov random chains are far better than all the previous ones, they are unable to match the performance of deep learning models for SISR. This study examines the Residual Dense Networks architecture proposed by Yhang et al. and analyzes the importance of its components. By leveraging hierarchical features from original low-resolution (LR) images, this architecture achieves superior performance, with a network structure comprising four main blocks, including the residual dense block (RDB) as the core. Through investigations of each block and analyses using various loss metrics, the study evaluates the effectiveness of the architecture and compares it to other state-of-the-art models that differ in both architecture and components.

claims.text: Residual Dense Networks for single image super-resolution utilize hierarchical features from low-resolution images through a structure comprising shallow feature extraction, residual dense blocks, dense feature fusion, and upsampling blocks, achieving superior performance compared to state-of-the-art models.

Residual Dense Blocks in the Residual Dense Network architecture employ local residual learning, local feature fusion, and a continuous memory mechanism to extract dense features and preserve local information effectively.

Global feature fusion and global residual learning in the Dense Feature Fusion block of the Residual Dense Network enable the adaptive combination of hierarchical features from residual dense blocks, improving super-resolution performance.
The Residual Dense Network architecture processes all features in low-resolution space, which enhances computational efficiency and performance for single image super-resolution tasks.

Ablation studies on the Residual Dense Network demonstrate that local dense connections and local residual learning are critical for achieving high performance in single image super-resolution, while global residual learning has a lesser impact.

similar_papers.title: Research on high-quality image super-resolution reconstruction algorithm based on deep convolutional generative adversarial network
similar_papers.abstract: Image is the main carrier of information transmission and presentation today, and high-quality image provides a solid foundation for the development of computer vision field because of its clear picture quality and rich details. In this paper, we take deep learning technology as the basis and optimize the image super-resolution reconstruction algorithm with targeted training, adopt enhanced generative adversarial network, and combine the image cross-level self-similarity features to construct a high-quality image super-resolution reconstruction model based on deep convolutional generative adversarial network. Simulation results show that the algorithm proposed in this paper has better performance, the objective evaluation indexes of the reconstructed image are significantly improved, and the operation speed is relatively fast, the recovered image has more high-frequency detail information, and the visual effect is better.

claims.text: A high-quality image super-resolution reconstruction model based on Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (DCGAN) combined with Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (ESRGAN) and cross-level self-similarity features of 3D-MRI images improves visual quality and texture details of reconstructed images.

The ESRGAN-based model utilizes perceptual loss, adversarial loss, and content loss to enhance high-frequency details and brightness in reconstructed images, resulting in sharper edges and richer textures.

The optimized ESRGAN-R model achieves faster convergence and higher reconstruction efficiency compared to the original ESRGAN, making it suitable for applications requiring high reconstruction speed and visual quality.
The ESRWGAN-R model, which incorporates Wasserstein loss, achieves the highest reconstruction accuracy among tested models, making it suitable for applications prioritizing precision over speed.

Cross-level self-similarity in 3D-MRI images is leveraged to expand training datasets and improve the performance of super-resolution reconstruction models by utilizing three-dimensional feature information.

similar_papers.title: Super-resolution single-molecule reconstruction of composite infrared images based on deep machine learning
similar_papers.abstract: In order to improve the resolution of infrared images of single-molecule reconstruction of composite materials, this paper proposes an image super-resolution reconstruction method based on deep machine learning SRGAN, By replacing the residual blocks of the generated network in SRGAN with residual dense block, it can more effectively acquire and utilize the image features from various network layers, especially those containing high-frequency information, thereby ensuring that more details and textures are preserved during the magnification of infrared images. The SE attention mechanism is incorporated into the generative network by assigning a weight to each channel, which strengthens the focus on important features while reducing reliance on irrelevant information. Super-resolution reconstruction experiments conducted on CFRP composite material infrared images demonstrate that the improved algorithm achieves a 0.6 increase in Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and a 0.3% increase in Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) compared to SRGAN, providing valuable references for the super-resolution reconstruction of infrared images of composite materials.

claims.text: Replacing residual blocks with residual dense blocks in the generator network of SRGAN improves the extraction and utilization of high-frequency image features, preserving more details and textures during infrared image super-resolution reconstruction.

Incorporating the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism into the SRGAN framework enhances the focus on important features while reducing reliance on irrelevant information, improving the quality of reconstructed infrared images.
Removing batch normalization layers from the SRGAN generative network improves generalization ability, reduces computational cost, and enhances performance in infrared image super-resolution tasks.

The improved SRGAN model achieves superior performance in infrared image reconstruction tasks compared to traditional SRGAN, with notable advancements in Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM).
The enhanced SRGAN framework provides significant engineering value for defect detection in composite materials by improving the resolution and quality of infrared images.

similar_papers.title: Enhancing Single-Image Super-Resolution using Patch-Mosaic Data Augmentation on Lightweight Bimodal Network
similar_papers.abstract: With the advancement of deep learning, single-image super-resolution (SISR) has made significant strides. However, most current SISR methods are challenging to employ in real-world applications because they are doubtlessly employed by substantial computational and memory costs caused by complex operations. Furthermore, an efficient dataset is a key factor for bettering model training. The hybrid models of CNN and Vision Transformer can be more efficient in the SISR task. Nevertheless, they require substantial or extremely high-quality datasets for training that could be unavailable from time to time. To tackle these issues, a solution combined by applying a Lightweight Bimodal Network (LBNet) and Patch-Mosaic data augmentation method which is the enhancement of CutMix and YOCO is proposed in this research. With patch-oriented Mosaic data augmentation, an efficient Symmetric CNN is utilized for local feature extraction and coarse image restoration. Plus, a Recursive Transformer aids in fully grasping the long-term dependence of images, enabling the global information to be fully used to refine texture details. Extensive experiments have shown that LBNet with the proposed data augmentation with zero-free additional parameters method outperforms the original LBNet and other state-of-the-art techniques in which image-level data augmentation is applied.

claims.text: The Patch-Mosaic data augmentation method, which combines patch-level image augmentation with mosaic-generating techniques, enhances the performance of single-image super-resolution models by increasing dataset diversity at both local and global levels without adding computational overhead.

The Lightweight Bimodal Network (LBNet) integrates a Symmetric CNN for local feature extraction and a Recursive Transformer for capturing long-term image dependencies, achieving efficient and high-quality image reconstruction in single-image super-resolution tasks.

The Symmetric CNN in LBNet employs paired parameter-sharing Local Feature Fusion Modules and channel attention mechanisms to optimize local feature extraction and utilization for image super-resolution.

The Recursive Transformer in LBNet uses a recursive mechanism to fully train the Transformer, enabling efficient learning of global image dependencies without significantly increasing model parameters or GPU memory consumption.

The Patch-Mosaic data augmentation method improves the performance of LBNet on standard single-image super-resolution benchmark datasets compared to image-level augmentation methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing lightweight models.

claims.text: A single image super-resolution model using highway connections with a non-linear gating mechanism can effectively mitigate gradient vanishing and exploding problems, stabilize training, and enhance the recovery of high-frequency details in reconstructed images.

Replacing local residual connections with highway connections in deep learning architectures for single image super-resolution enables faster and more stable convergence while reducing issues such as dying ReLU and gradient exploding.

The use of a gating mechanism in highway connections allows selective regulation of information flow, improving the discriminative learning ability and enhancing the reconstruction of fine image details.

Highway connection-based models for single image super-resolution achieve competitive performance on standard benchmarks and are less prone to common training issues compared to models using skip connections.
The proposed highway connection-based architecture is suitable for real-time and mobile applications due to its robust and efficient design.

similar_papers.title: Learning-Based Quality Assessment for Image Super-Resolution
similar_papers.abstract: Image Super-Resolution (SR) techniques improve visual quality by enhancing the spatial resolution of images. Quality evaluation metrics play a critical role in comparing and optimizing SR algorithms, but current metrics achieve only limited success, largely due to the lack of large-scale quality databases, which are essential for learning accurate and robust SR quality metrics. In this work, we first build a large-scale SR image database using a novel semi-automatic labeling approach, which allows us to label a large number of images with manageable human workload. The resulting SR Image quality database with Semi-Automatic Ratings (SISAR), so far the largest of SR-IQA database, contains 12 600 images of 100 natural scenes. We train an end-to-end Deep Image SR Quality (DISQ) model by employing two-stream Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) for feature extraction, followed by a feature fusion network for quality prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art metrics and achieves promising generalization performance in cross-database tests. The SISAR database and DISQ model will be made publicly available to facilitate reproducible research.

claims.text: A large-scale image super-resolution quality database, named SISAR, was developed using a novel semi-automatic labeling approach, containing 8,400 images of 100 natural scenes with reduced human labeling workload.

A two-stream deep neural network model, called DISQ, was designed for image super-resolution quality assessment, which extracts features from both high-resolution and low-resolution images, performs feature fusion, and predicts quality scores in an end-to-end manner.
The proposed DISQ model demonstrates superior performance compared to state-of-the-art image quality assessment metrics and exhibits strong generalization capabilities in cross-database evaluations.

The semi-automatic labeling method for the SISAR database leverages an observed exponential decay behavior in subjective quality scores during iterative downsampling and super-resolution processes, significantly reducing the need for extensive human labeling.

The feature fusion method in the DISQ model, which combines high-resolution and low-resolution image features through subtraction, enhances the model's ability to predict image quality with high correlation to human subjective scores.

similar_papers.title: A Two-Branch Multiscale Residual Attention Network for Single Image Super-Resolution in Remote Sensing Imagery
similar_papers.abstract: High-resolution remote sensing imagery finds applications in diverse fields, such as land-use mapping, crop planning, and disaster surveillance. To offer detailed and precise insights, reconstructing edges, textures, and other features is crucial. Despite recent advances in detail enhancement through deep learning, disparities between original and reconstructed images persist. To address this challenge, we propose a two-branch multiscale residual attention network for single-image super-resolution reconstruction. The network gathers complex information about input images from two branches with convolution layers of different kernel sizes. The two branches extract both low-level and high-level features from the input image. The network incorporates multiscale efficient channel attention and spatial attention blocks to capture channel and spatial dependencies in the feature maps. This results in more discriminative features and more accurate predictions. Moreover, residual modules with skip connections can help to overcome the vanishing gradient problem. We trained the proposed model on the WHU-RS19 dataset, collated from Google Earth satellite imagery, and validated it on the UC Merced, RSSCN7, AID, and real-world satellite datasets. The experimental results show that our network uses features at different levels of detail more effectively than state-of-the-art models.

claims.text: A two-branch multi-scale residual attention network (TBMRA) for single-image super-resolution reconstruction in remote sensing imagery is proposed, which uses convolution layers of different kernel sizes to extract low-level and high-level features, incorporates multi-scale efficient channel attention and spatial attention blocks to capture channel and spatial dependencies, and employs residual modules with skip connections to address the vanishing gradient problem.

The TBMRA network is trained on the WHU-RS19 dataset and validated on UC Merced, RSSCN7, AID, and real-world satellite datasets, demonstrating superior performance in capturing and preserving salient image information compared to state-of-the-art methods.

The hybrid multi-scale attention mechanism in the TBMRA network combines efficient channel attention and spatial attention to extract global features and emphasize important regions, improving the reconstruction of high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs.

The TBMRA network employs local and global residual connections to enhance model stability and feature retention, enabling the extraction of both fine-grained and larger-scale features for improved super-resolution performance.

Experimental results show that the TBMRA network achieves higher PSNR, SSIM, and lower LPIPS values compared to existing state-of-the-art methods, while maintaining a favorable balance between model performance and inference time, and demonstrating effectiveness on real-world satellite imagery.

similar_papers.title: Cartoon single-image super-resolution approach based on generative adversarial network
similar_papers.abstract: In recent years, the study of a single image super-resolution (SISR) is crucial to improving image resolution and using hardware technology to improve image resolution. SISR is widely used in satellite remote sensing, video surveillance, and medical image processing because it mainly relies on deep learning algorithms to realize the conversion from low-resolution (LR) images to high-resolution images. It has the advantages of low cost, simple operation, and high efficiency. This paper proposes an image super-resolution method based on a generative adversarial network named text localization generative adversarial nets (TLGAN) model. The method is improved based on super-resolution generative adversarial networks (SRGAN), and the batch normalization layer is removed, which significantly reduces the computational burden of the model. In TLGAN model, we used the transfer learning method to pre-trained the model on the large dataset ImageNet, and then apply the pre-trained model to the cartoon image data set animes to achieve image super-resolution. Experimental results report that the proposed method has the advantages of fast running speed and excellent visual perception of super-resolution images compared with bicubic interpolation and SRGAN method.

claims.text: A single-image super-resolution method named Transform Learning Generative Adversarial Network (TLGAN) improves upon the Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (SRGAN) by removing the batch normalization layer to reduce computational burden and employing transfer learning with pre-training on the ImageNet dataset for enhanced performance on cartoon image datasets.

The TLGAN model uses a pre-trained VGG19 network to extract high-frequency image features, accelerates model convergence, and mitigates issues such as gradient disappearance and explosion during training.

The TLGAN model achieves superior visual perception quality for super-resolution images of cartoon datasets compared to bicubic interpolation and SRGAN, producing images with clear outlines, natural textures, and reduced artifacts and aliasing.

The TLGAN model demonstrates robustness in super-resolution tasks across multiple cartoon datasets, including Anime-characters, Simpsons-characters, and Anime-face, despite lower PSNR and SSIM scores compared to bicubic interpolation and SRGAN.
The TLGAN model incorporates a PReLU activation function and deep residual modules instead of batch normalization to retain extensive feature maps and reduce feature loss during training.

similar_papers.title: Image quality assessment for determining efficacy and limitations of Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Network (SRCNN)
similar_papers.abstract: Traditional metrics for evaluating the efficacy of image processing techniques do not lend themselves to under- standing the capabilities and limitations of modern image processing methods - particularly those enabled by deep learning. When applying image processing in engineering solutions, a scientist or engineer has a need to justify their design decisions with clear metrics. By applying blind/referenceless image spatial quality (BRISQUE), Structural SIMilarity (SSIM) index scores, and Peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) to images before and after im- age processing, we can quantify quality improvements in a meaningful way and determine the lowest recoverable image quality for a given method.

claims.text: The Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Network (SRCNN) improves image quality metrics such as BRISQUE, SSIM, and PSNR for images degraded by bicubic interpolation, but its efficacy diminishes with higher scaling factors and successive reconstruction passes.
SRCNN reconstruction enhances the 'naturalness' of images as measured by the BRISQUE metric, but is less effective at correcting JPEG compression artifacts, which produce erratic BRISQUE scores.
Incremental upsampling using SRCNN with smaller scaling factors (e.g., 2x2x) yields better image quality and sharper details compared to single-shot upsampling with larger scaling factors (e.g., 4x).
The BRISQUE metric demonstrates strong correlation with human judgment of image quality and is effective for evaluating the restoration of natural scene statistics in images processed by SRCNN.

SRCNN reconstruction introduces edge-ringing artifacts after multiple passes, attributed to the Gibbs phenomenon, which progressively approximates discontinuous functions and degrades image 'naturalness' as measured by BRISQUE.

similar_papers.title: A Cosine Network for Image Super-Resolution
similar_papers.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks can use hierarchical information to progressively extract structural information to recover high-quality images. However, preserving the effectiveness of the obtained structural information is important in image super-resolution. In this paper, we propose a cosine network for image super-resolution (CSRNet) by improving a network architecture and optimizing the training strategy. To extract complementary homologous structural information, odd and even heterogeneous blocks are designed to enlarge the architectural differences and improve the performance of image super-resolution. Combining linear and non-linear structural information can overcome the drawback of homologous information and enhance the robustness of the obtained structural information in image super-resolution. Taking into account the local minimum of gradient descent, a cosine annealing mechanism is used to optimize the training procedure by performing warm restarts and adjusting the learning rate. Experimental results illustrate that the proposed CSRNet is competitive with state-of-the-art methods in image super-resolution.

claims.text: A cosine network for single image super-resolution, termed CSRNet, utilizes odd and even heterogeneous blocks to extract complementary homologous and heterogeneous structural information, improving the robustness and quality of recovered images.

The cosine annealing mechanism optimizes the training process by dynamically adjusting the learning rate, preventing local minima in gradient descent and enhancing the learning ability of the super-resolution model.

Odd enhancement blocks in CSRNet use parallel and serial asymmetric convolutional layers combined with ReLU activation to extract complementary homologous and heterogeneous structural information for image super-resolution.

Even enhancement blocks in CSRNet employ stacked identical convolutional layers, ReLU activation, and residual learning to refine hierarchical structural information and improve super-resolution performance.

CSRNet achieves competitive performance in single image super-resolution compared to state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmark datasets and scaling factors, demonstrating its effectiveness in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations.

similar_papers.title: Hand-drawn Illustration Design in National Wave Style Based on Deep Learning and Image Super Resolution Reconstruction
similar_papers.abstract: This research presents a novel framework, Deep Learning based Super Resolution Reconstruction (DESRR), for the creation of hand-drawn illustrations in a specific National Wave Style. The proposed framework leverages advanced deep learning techniques, with a primary focus on the integration of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for image super resolution reconstruction. The objective is to enhance the resolution and fidelity of hand-drawn illustrations while preserving the distinctive characteristics of the chosen national wave style. The DESRR framework involves a two-step process: firstly, the utilization of GAN algorithms for generating illustrations that encapsulate the unique artistic nuances of the targeted national wave style; and secondly, the application of image super resolution techniques to refine and elevate the quality of the generated illustrations. The GAN-based approach, specifically inspired by ESRGAN (Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network), enables the model to learn intricate details and textures, ensuring that the reconstructed images maintain the authenticity of the chosen style. To implement DESRR, a curated dataset of hand-drawn images in the specified national wave style is employed for training. The model is fine-tuned to strike a balance between increased resolution and the faithful representation of the targeted artistic style. The framework’s effectiveness is evaluated through a comprehensive analysis, considering both quantitative measures of image quality and qualitative assessments of style preservation. The proposed DESRR framework not only contributes to the field of artistic illustration design but also showcases the potential of combining deep learning and image super resolution techniques for creative applications.

claims.text: The Deep Learning based Super Resolution Reconstruction (DESRR) framework integrates Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (ESRGAN) techniques to create high-resolution hand-drawn illustrations while preserving the distinctive characteristics of a specific National Wave Style.

The DESRR framework employs a two-step process where GANs generate synthetic hand-drawn illustrations that replicate the unique features of a curated dataset, followed by ESRGAN-based image super-resolution techniques to enhance the resolution and visual fidelity of the illustrations.

The DESRR framework is validated using a curated dataset of hand-drawn images in the National Wave Style, including the iconic Japanese artwork 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa,' to ensure the preservation of cultural and artistic authenticity.

The DESRR framework demonstrates the potential of combining deep learning and image super-resolution techniques to enhance the quality and detail of traditional artistic styles for creative applications.

The DESRR framework achieves a balance between increasing image resolution and maintaining the artistic nuances of the National Wave Style, as evaluated through quantitative image quality metrics and qualitative style preservation assessments.

anchor_claims.text: An image quality assessment (IQA)-guided single image super-resolution (SISR) method using deep learning networks achieves a balance between perceptual quality and distortion measures by integrating an IQA network to guide the adjustment of super-resolution network parameters.

The proposed method introduces an interactive training mechanism via a cascaded network, where the IQA network acts as a supervisor in constructing the loss function of the super-resolution network, addressing the issue of heterogeneous datasets used by IQA and SR networks.

A pairwise ranking hinge loss method is proposed to dynamically create training labels, overcoming the challenge of insufficient training samples and preventing overfitting during the training process.
The proposed method demonstrates a better tradeoff between perceptual quality and distortion measures compared to recent SISR methods, as evidenced by extensive benchmark experiments and analyses.

The architecture of the proposed method is flexible and not confined to a specific network model, allowing the baseline of the super-resolution network to be adjusted according to practical requirements, such as improving performance or enhancing efficiency.

**Summary:**

Recent advances in single-image super-resolution (SISR) have been significantly enhanced by integrating deep learning image quality assessment (IQA) frameworks into the super-resolution pipeline. These IQA-guided deep learning networks, such as the Image Quality Assessment-Guided Deep Learning Network (IQA-GDLN) family, leverage dedicated IQA models to evaluate the perceptual quality of low-resolution inputs or reconstructions. The IQA modules often extract nuanced features from high- and low-frequency image maps, typically utilizing frequency-domain representations or multi-stream architectures (e.g., high and low frequency streams), and employ loss functions like pairwise ranking hinge loss to dynamically guide the super-resolution network. By fusing IQA feedback, these architectures can optimize the balance between restored sharpness and visual fidelity, preventing overfitting and addressing the inherent challenges posed by mismatched datasets and loss objectives between IQA and SR components. 

Cascaded or interactive training strategies allow IQA networks to supervise SR network parameter updates or the construction of combined loss functions, enhancing the performance and robustness of SISR systems. Modern methods extend beyond traditional metrics (such as PSNR, SSIM) by incorporating perceptually relevant measures like the no-reference IDP score, which better reflects human judgments in super-resolved images, especially for medical (MRI) or natural images.

Below is a consolidated summary of the supplied research context, focusing on how deep learning, single-image super-resolution (SISR), and image quality assessment (IQA) increasingly interact as parts of a unified reconstruction and evaluation framework.

Summary: Deep Learning-Based SISR and Image Quality Assessment

Single-image super-resolution (SISR) aims to reconstruct a high-resolution (HR) image from a single low-resolution (LR) observation. Because this reconstruction is inherently ill-posed, multiple plausible HR images can correspond to the same LR input. Deep learning has substantially improved SISR by learning nonlinear LR-to-HR mappings and progressively incorporating residual learning, dense connections, attention, Transformers, adversarial learning, and multi-scale feature extraction.

Early CNN-based approaches such as SRCNN demonstrated that feature extraction, nonlinear mapping, and image reconstruction could be jointly optimized in an end-to-end network. Subsequent residual architectures, particularly EDSR, improved reconstruction accuracy by removing unnecessary batch-normalization layers, introducing residual scaling, and adopting effective loss functions such as L1 loss. Dense and attention-based networks further strengthened the extraction of high-frequency information, while CNN-Transformer hybrid architectures combined CNNs' ability to recover local texture with Transformers' capacity to model long-range dependencies. Lightweight approaches additionally employ grouped convolution, re-parameterization, knowledge distillation, recursive structures, and efficient attention to reduce computational requirements.

A central challenge is that maximizing conventional distortion measures such as PSNR and SSIM does not necessarily produce images with the best perceptual quality. GAN-based and perceptual-loss approaches can generate sharper, visually appealing textures but sometimes obtain lower pixel-wise scores or introduce artificial details. Consequently, modern SISR research increasingly considers a perception-distortion tradeoff, using PSNR and SSIM together with perceptually oriented measures such as LPIPS and no-reference image quality indicators.

An important development is the direct integration of Image Quality Assessment (IQA) into the SISR learning process. In an IQA-guided cascaded framework, an IQA network is not merely used after reconstruction to evaluate the output. Instead, it operates as a supervisor for the SR network, contributing to the construction of its training objective and guiding parameter optimization toward perceptually preferable reconstructions. This interactive mechanism helps reconcile the heterogeneous datasets normally used to train SR and IQA models. Pairwise ranking with a hinge-based loss can dynamically construct supervisory labels, addressing limited IQA training samples and helping reduce overfitting. Because the IQA component can guide different SR backbones, this framework is also adaptable to networks selected either for maximum reconstruction quality or computational efficiency.

IQA itself has evolved toward deep, task-specific assessment of super-resolved imagery. Rather than relying exclusively on reference images, no-reference approaches can learn quality representations directly from reconstructed images. For example, frequency-aware assessment separates an SR image into high- and low-frequency maps, allowing a two-stream deep network to independently analyze fine details, edges and structural information. Features from complementary network levels can then be fused and regressed into an overall quality prediction. Cross-database evaluations indicate that such approaches can generalize beyond individual SR quality datasets.

Other learning-based IQA architectures exploit relationships between LR and SR images. The DISQ framework, for example, uses a two-stream network to extract information from both resolutions and combines the representations to predict perceived image quality. Large-scale dedicated SR quality databases such as SISAR further enable learning quality models that correlate more closely with subjective human judgments. These approaches demonstrate that quality assessment tailored specifically to super-resolution artifacts can provide information that conventional generic metrics may miss.

The literature also demonstrates that effective SISR depends on several complementary design principles:

Residual and dense learning improve gradient propagation and retention of hierarchical features.
Attention mechanisms emphasize informative channels, spatial regions, edges, and high-frequency structures.
CNN-Transformer hybrids jointly capture local image characteristics and global dependencies.
Multi-scale processing supports reconstruction across different spatial structures and magnification factors.
Perceptual, adversarial, edge, L1, Charbonnier, and IQA-guided losses offer alternatives to optimizing pixel-wise error alone.
No-reference and learned IQA provide more realistic assessments when ground-truth HR images are unavailable.
Efficient architectures, including grouped convolution, parameter sharing, re-parameterization, and distillation, improve suitability for real-time or edge deployment.
Domain-specific SR extends these concepts to remote sensing, MRI, infrared imaging, holographic microscopy, and artistic imagery.
Overall Research Trend

The literature collectively indicates a transition from “reconstruct first, assess afterward” toward quality-aware reconstruction, where image quality assessment becomes part of the learning loop:

Low-resolution image → SR deep network → reconstructed image → learned IQA network → perceptual-quality feedback → SR parameter optimization

This integration is particularly important because high numerical fidelity and high perceptual quality are not always equivalent. An IQA-guided deep SISR network can therefore optimize reconstruction according to both distortion and perceptual objectives rather than treating PSNR or SSIM as the sole measures of success.

Overall, the research suggests that the next generation of SISR systems should combine powerful reconstruction architectures with learned, perceptually meaningful quality assessment. Flexible IQA-guided optimization, robust no-reference assessment, efficient architectures, and quality metrics aligned with human perception provide a promising route toward SR models that recover fine structural detail while maintaining natural appearance, generalization, and practical computational efficiency.

An important theme across these studies is the perception-distortion trade-off. Optimizing exclusively for pixel-wise losses such as MSE or L1 can favor high PSNR/SSIM but may yield visually smooth reconstruction. Conversely, perceptual and adversarial objectives can produce sharper, more realistic-looking images while sometimes lowering conventional fidelity scores or introducing artificial texture. Consequently, contemporary SISR research increasingly combines complementary losses and evaluates models with multiple fidelity, structural, perceptual, and sometimes human-subjective quality measures.

The literature also emphasizes efficiency and generalization. Lightweight networks, grouped convolutions, parameter sharing, recursive modules, arbitrary-scale reconstruction, attention mechanisms, data augmentation, and model re-parameterization attempt to reduce computational cost without substantially sacrificing reconstruction quality. Domain-specific studies demonstrate that these principles extend beyond natural photographs to remote-sensing, MRI, infrared, holographic, and illustration data, although appropriate quality measures can differ markedly between domains.

Overall, the supplied evidence suggests that progress in SISR depends not only on designing stronger reconstruction networks but also on developing reliable image-quality assessment strategies aligned with human perception and application requirements. A robust evaluation framework should therefore combine distortion measures such as PSNR and SSIM with perceptual or learned IQA measures, visual assessment, and, where necessary, domain-specific criteria.

Answer:
Summary: Single-Image Super-Resolution, Image Quality Assessment, and Deep Learning Networks

Deep learning-based single-image super-resolution (SISR) reconstructs a high-resolution image from a single low-resolution input. Modern approaches have progressed from convolutional architectures such as SRCNN to residual, attention-based, GAN, and Transformer-based networks. These models improve feature extraction, recover high-frequency details, and model increasingly complex local and global image dependencies. However, because SISR is inherently ill-posed, optimizing conventional distortion measures such as PSNR and SSIM does not necessarily produce images with the best perceived visual quality. This has made image quality assessment (IQA) an important component of SISR research.

A key research direction is integrating learned IQA directly with super-resolution training. Rather than treating quality assessment solely as a post-processing evaluation step, an IQA network can provide perceptual supervision to the SR network, helping optimize reconstructed images toward a better balance between pixel-level fidelity and perceptual quality. Related research also uses no-reference or learned quality models that extract quality-sensitive information from features such as high- and low-frequency image components. Such approaches can complement traditional metrics and better characterize artifacts, sharpness, textures, and structural fidelity.

Across the broader literature, several architectural strategies support improved SISR quality:

Residual and dense connections facilitate training of deep networks and preserve hierarchical image information.
Attention mechanisms selectively emphasize informative spatial regions and feature channels.
CNN-Transformer hybrids combine CNN-based recovery of local textures with Transformer-based modeling of long-range dependencies.
Perceptual, edge, adversarial, and reconstruction losses allow networks to optimize different aspects of visual fidelity.
Lightweight and multi-scale architectures seek to retain reconstruction quality while reducing parameters and inference cost.
Quality-aware training and learned IQA provide alternatives to relying exclusively on PSNR or SSIM when perceptual realism is important.

Overall, the literature suggests that SISR is increasingly moving from maximizing a single distortion metric toward joint optimization of reconstruction accuracy, perceptual quality, and computational efficiency. Learned IQA provides a particularly promising mechanism for supplying quality-aware feedback during training and for evaluating super-resolved images when no perfect reference is available.

Deep-learning SISR seeks not merely to enlarge an image, but to reconstruct plausible high-frequency information while retaining fidelity to the source.
