claims.text: A fault filtering method for heterogeneous wireless sensor networks (HWSN) was developed, which uses normalized distance estimations based on the communication radius of nodes and the Jenks Natural Breaks algorithm to filter out faulty reference nodes, improving the localization accuracy of existing hop-based localization algorithms.

The fault filtering method replaces Average Hop Distance (AHD) with Average Communication Distance (ACD), calculated as a function of the communication radius of nodes, to mitigate the effects of node heterogeneity on distance estimations in HWSN.

The Jenks Natural Breaks algorithm is employed in the fault filtering method to identify and exclude nodes producing inconsistent distance estimations, thereby enhancing the accuracy of localization in HWSN.

The fault filtering method was tested with DV-Hop, Weighted DV-Hop, and Harris Hawks Optimization-based Area Minimization (HHO-AM) algorithms in 2D/3D, isotropic/anisotropic environments, showing improvements in localization accuracy by 14%, 52%, and 51%, respectively.

The computational complexity of the fault filtering method is O(k × L^2), where k is the number of classes and L is the number of reference nodes, and it adds minimal overhead to the existing hop-based localization algorithms.

similar_papers.title: Coverage Control Algorithm-Based Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization and Node Sleeping in Wireless Multimedia Sensor Networks
similar_papers.abstract: Wireless multimedia sensor networks (WMSNs) are widely used in various fields where coverage control is a critical difficulty because multiple requirements need to be considered such as service quality and energy consumption. In this paper, we focus on the issues existing in coverage model and coverage control method, and propose an adaptive particle swarm optimization algorithm for solving the coverage control problem in the WMSNs. First of all, a 3D coverage model is developed with introducing the perceptual radius of sensors, while the optimal projection area of a single sensor is deduced. Hereafter, an adaptive particle swarm optimization is suggested to optimize the location information of sensors for reducing both perceptual overlapping areas and perceptual blind areas in the monitoring area. At last, a redundant node sleeping strategy is presented to reduce the number of working sensors. Simulation results have show that we can ensure better coverage as well as fewer sensors compared to the state-of-the-art frameworks.

An adaptive particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed to optimize the location information of sensors in wireless multimedia sensor networks, reducing perceptual overlapping areas and blind spots in the monitored area to improve coverage.
A redundant node sleeping strategy is introduced to minimize the number of active sensors in wireless multimedia sensor networks, thereby reducing energy consumption while maintaining high coverage.

The proposed adaptive particle swarm optimization algorithm incorporates an adaptive weight and enhanced learning factors to balance global exploration and local exploitation, improving the algorithm's convergence and performance in high-dimensional optimization problems.

Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher coverage with fewer working sensors compared to state-of-the-art methods, effectively addressing the trade-off between coverage and energy consumption in wireless multimedia sensor networks.

similar_papers.title: Game theory based adaptive transmit power control algorithm for IoT wireless sensor networks
similar_papers.abstract:
Objectives: To design a transmission power control (TPC) algorithm for the Internet of Things (IoT) based Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) such that the energy cost is reduced and the expected throughput is increased. Method: In this study, a Game theory based adaptive transmit power control (GT-ATPC) algorithm for IoT-WSN is proposed. In this algorithm, for each sender, the initial transmission power level (TPL) is determined from the difference of Received Signal Strength (RSS) measurements at the base station (BS). The TPL is adaptively adjusted by means of Game theory. For each sender, the expected throughput, energy cost and connectivity values are estimated from which a utility function is derived. Findings: By simulation results, it has been shown that GT-ATPC attains 37% higher throughput with 57% reduced energy cost and 30% lesser overhead when compared with GTS-PM approach. Novelty: The TPL of a node is adjusted based on the estimated values of utility function such that the throughput and connectivity is high and energy cost is less. 
Keywords: Internet of Things (IoT); wireless sensor network (WSN); transmission power; Energy cost; game theory; utility function

anchor_claims.text: A fault location measurement method for sensor nodes based on a fuzzy control algorithm reduces energy consumption and measurement time compared to traditional methods by utilizing cluster head nodes to directly measure the fault location of member nodes within each cluster.

The fuzzy control algorithm determines the probability of a node being selected as a cluster head and its competition radius based on residual energy, node centrality, node degree, and distance from the sink node, optimizing clustering in wireless sensor networks.

The proposed fault location measurement method integrates fuzzy control algorithms with neural networks, using preprocessing and symptom reduction to enhance fault diagnosis accuracy in wireless sensor networks.

Radial basis function neural networks are employed in the fault location measurement method to process reduced fault symptom sets, leveraging Gaussian functions for nonlinear transformation and linear optimization for efficient learning.

Simulation experiments demonstrate that the fault location measurement method based on fuzzy control algorithms achieves lower measurement error and shorter measurement time compared to traditional methods, improving performance in large-scale wireless sensor networks.

**Summary of Fault Location Measurement in Sensor Nodes Using Fuzzy Control Algorithms in Wireless Sensor Networks**

Recent advances in fault location measurement for wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have increasingly incorporated fuzzy control algorithms to address the challenges of energy efficiency, fast fault detection, and accuracy in distributed environments. These methods leverage the adaptive reasoning capabilities of fuzzy logic to handle the inherent uncertainties and variations present in sensor node data and network conditions. 

In particular, a common approach involves employing cluster-based hierarchical structures where cluster heads directly measure or estimate the location of faulty nodes within their clusters, thereby reducing the need for redundant or inefficient routing to remote base stations. The fuzzy control algorithm dynamically selects optimal cluster heads based on critical factors such as residual energy, node centrality (degree and position), distance to base station, and load. This optimized node selection helps balance energy consumption, maintain load distribution, and improve fault localization speed.

Additionally, the fuzzy logic framework is often combined with other optimization techniques (e.g., neural networks, swarm intelligence algorithms, or metaheuristics) to enhance fault diagnosis accuracy. These combinations facilitate preprocessing of fault symptoms and reduction of redundant data, leading to more precise fault identification and localization. The resulting method typically achieves lower measurement errors and shorter detection times compared to traditional centralized or simple distributed approaches.

Simulation and experimental studies consistently demonstrate improved network performance with these fuzzy-based fault location techniques, including reduced energy depletion of sensor nodes, increased network lifetime, fewer node failures, and higher fault detection success rates, especially in large or dynamically changing WSNs. Furthermore, the use of fuzzy control supports real-time adaptation to changing network states and environmental conditions, making it particularly suitable for mission-critical and energy-constrained wireless sensor applications. Overall, the integration of fuzzy control algorithms in fault location measurement for sensor nodes represents a significant step forward in developing efficient, reliable, and scalable fault management solutions for wireless sensor networks.

similar_papers.title: Cardiac arrhythmia detection using dual-tree wavelet transform and convolutional neural network
similar_papers.abstract: The non-stationary ECG signals are used as key tools in screening coronary diseases. ECG recording is collected from millions of cardiac cells and depolarization and re-polarization conducted in a synchronized manner as: the P wave occurs first, followed by the QRS-complex and the T wave, which will repeat in each beat. The signal is altered in a cardiac beat period for different heart conditions. This change can be observed in order to diagnose the patient’s heart status. Simple naked eye diagnosis can mislead the detection. At that point, computer-assisted diagnosis (CAD) is therefore required. In this paper dual-tree wavelet transform is used as a feature extraction technique along with deep learning (DL)-based convolution neural network (CNN) to detect abnormal heart. The findings of this research and associated studies are without any cumbersome artificial environments. This work investigates the viability of using deep learning-based architectures for heartbeat classification. The DL architecture is used for the proposed project, and the results suggest that it is feasible to use 2D images to train a deep learning architectures for heartbeat classification. The CNN produced the highest overall accuracy of around 99%. The CAD method proposed has high generalizability; it can help doctors efficiently identify diseases and decrease misdiagnosis.

similar_papers.title: Accurate Cardiac Arrhythmia Detection Using Horse Herd Optimization Algorithm-Enhanced Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN-HOA)
similar_papers.abstract:
Cardiac arrhythmias are significant contributors to global mortality, necessitating precise and timely diagnosis based on electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. This paper introduces an advanced diagnostic system utilizing a deep 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture integrated with the Horse Herd Optimization Algorithm (HOA) for automated feature extraction and classification. The primary objective is to overcome the limitations of manual hyperparameter tuning by using the HOA metaheuristic search capability to optimally tune critical parameters, specifically the Learning Rate and Batch Size. In the proposed framework, raw ECG signals from the standard MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database are first preprocessed using the discrete wavelet transform with the "db6" mother wavelet to effectively suppress nonstationary noise and baseline wander. The denoised signals are then processed through a sequence of four convolutional blocks, featuring batch normalization and max-pooling, to extract hierarchical morphological features. Experimental results using 5-fold cross-validation demonstrate that the proposed CNN-HOA model achieves a state-of-the-art accuracy of 99.8%, with 99.9% sensitivity and specificity across five Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation beat types: normal (N), supraventricular (S), ventricular (V), fusion (F), and unknown (Q). This study validates that the synergistic integration of modern swarm intelligence algorithms with deep learning provides a robust and highly efficient solution for high-precision medical signal processing and clinical-grade automated diagnosis.

similar_papers.title: Complex-valued convolutional neural network with time-frequency representation for electrocardiogram-based arrhythmia detection
similar_papers.abstract: This research proposes an end-to-end procedure for arrhythmia detection based on electrocardiogram (ECG) signals using complex-valued convolutional neural network (CVCNN) incorporated with time-frequency representation. The proposed model leverages complex numbers to capture amplitude and phase information that enhances the ability of the model for detecting time-frequency variation in cardiac signals. First, signal preprocessing techniques---including normalization, wavelet denoising, and R-peak detection---are applied. Subsequently, the model extracts complex features from raw ECG data by employing the Hilbert transform to derive the analytic signal and the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) to generate a time–frequency representation. The proposed CVCNN framework effectively learns spatial-temporal features critical for detecting various types of arrhythmias. The method is evaluated using the Massachusetts Institute of Technology–Beth Israel Hospital (MIT–BIH) Arrhythmia Database. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance compared with real-valued CNNs and existing approaches for arrhythmia detection under the same evaluation protocol. Specifically, the proposed method obtained an accuracy of 99.74%, precision of 99.36%, recall of 99.30%, specificity of 99.84%, and F1-score of 99.36%. A 10-fold cross-validation scheme is employed to evaluate the model’s effectiveness, yielding superior performance relative to conventional methods. Overall, the proposed approach constitutes a competitive complex-valued learning framework for ECG-based arrhythmia classification under beat-level evaluation and offers a robust tool for artificial intelligence (AI)-based medical diagnostics.

similar_papers.title: A Novel Inter Patient ECG Arrhythmia Classification Approach with Deep Feature Extraction and 1D Convolutional Neural Network
similar_papers.abstract: —The World Health Organization (WHO) sheds light on the escalating prevalence of heart diseases, foreseeing a substantial rise in the years ahead, impacting a vast global population. Swift and accurate early detection becomes pivotal in managing severe complications, underscoring the urgency of timely identification. While Ventricular Ectopic Beats (V) might initially be considered normal, their frequent occurrence could serve as a potential red flag for progressing to severe conditions like atrial fibrillation, Ventricular Tachycardia, and even cardiac arrest. This accentuates the need for developing an automated approach for early detection of cardiovascular diseases (CVD). This paper presents a novel method to classify arrhythmias. Leveraging the Wavelet Scattering Transform (WST) to extract morphological features from Electrocardiogram heartbeats (ECG), these features seamlessly integrate into a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The CNN is finely tuned to distinguish between V, Supraventricular Ectopic Beats (S), and Non-Ectopic Beats (N). Our model's performance surpasses state-of-the-art models, boasting precision, sensitivity, and specificity of 94.56%, 97.26%, and 99.54% for V, and 99.25%, 98.65%, and 93.26% for N. claims.text: A novel method for classifying electrocardiogram (ECG) heartbeats into three categories—Normal (N), Supraventricular Ectopic Beats (S), and Ventricular Ectopic Beats (V)—was developed by combining Wavelet Scattering Transform (WST) for morphological feature extraction with a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for classification.

The Wavelet Scattering Transform (WST) was used to extract both time-domain and frequency-domain features from ECG signals, providing a robust and stable representation of signal characteristics while preserving 99% of the signal's energy in the second order of the scattering network.

The 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture, consisting of 11 layers, was designed to efficiently classify ECG heartbeats with reduced computational cost compared to 2D CNNs, while maintaining high classification accuracy.

The proposed method addresses class imbalance in the MIT-BIH arrhythmia dataset by employing the Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) to generate synthetic instances for underrepresented classes, improving classification performance for all heartbeat types.

The proposed model demonstrated superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, achieving an overall accuracy of 98.06% and high sensitivity, precision, and specificity for the N, S, and V heartbeat classes, with notable improvements in distinguishing Supraventricular Ectopic Beats (S).

similar_papers.title: A Dual-Channel Pine Wilt Disease Recognition Method with Discrete Wavelet Transform
similar_papers.abstract: Pine wilt disease is a significant global plant epidemic and a management priority for numerous countries worldwide. Pine wood nematodes can parasitize a wide range of pine species, making early detection of infected trees essential for preventing further spread of the disease. Recent advances in deep learning and remote sensing technologies have enabled efficient automated detection of diseased trees. Most existing methods rely on convolutional neural network layers for feature extraction and spatial dimension reduction, which may cause the loss of fine-grained texture details and lead to misdetection of background elements and visually similar objects. To enhance diseased tree recognition accuracy, this paper proposes an object detection model using images captured by unmanned aerial vehicles. The proposed method incorporates discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to reduce spatial resolution while preserving critical information for further analysis, and integrates a cross-modal channel enhancement module within a two-stream feature extraction network. Furthermore, the method incorporates a RoI-based similarity constraint that applies cosine similarity loss and classification supervision to ensure coherent feature representations between processing branches. This approach achieves 89.2% accuracy on the pine wilt disease dataset and outperforms advanced methods on the VisDrone dataset. Several object detection models are compared based on the mean average precision (mAP) metric. Results demonstrate that the DWT-based detection algorithm achieves superior performance in detecting individual small targets and clustered infected pine trees.

claims.text: A dual-channel object detection model for pine wilt disease recognition integrates a conventional convolutional neural network pathway with a discrete wavelet transform channel, enabling complementary feature fusion from spatial and frequency-domain representations.

The discrete wavelet transform module in the proposed model reduces spatial resolution while preserving fine-grained texture details, improving the detection of small and clustered infected pine trees in UAV imagery.

A cross-modal channel enhancement module in the dual-channel network improves feature representation by leveraging channel-wise interactions and mutual information sharing between spatial and frequency-domain features.

An object-level similarity loss mechanism, combining cosine similarity constraints and classification supervision, ensures coherent and discriminative feature representations across dual processing branches, reducing false detections in complex backgrounds.

The proposed detection framework, which incorporates inverse discrete wavelet transform for multi-scale feature refinement, demonstrates superior performance in detecting small and clustered objects compared to state-of-the-art methods on both the pine wilt disease dataset and the VisDrone dataset.

similar_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a Neural Network classifier model for the automatic identification of the ventricular and supraventricular arrhythmias cardiac arrhythmias. The wavelet transform (DWT) and dual tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT) is applied for QRS complex detec-tion. After segmentation both feature of DWT and DTCWT is combined for feature extraction, statistical feature has been calculated to re-duce the overhead of classifier. An adaptive filtering with the soft computed wavelet thersholding to the signals before the extraction is done in pre-processing. Different ECG database is considered to evaluate the propose work with MIT-BIH database Normal Sinus Rhythm Da-tabase (NSRD) , and MIT-BIH Supraventricular Arrhythmia Database (svdb) .The evaluated outcomes of ECG classification claims 98 -99 % of accuracy under different training and testing situation.

claims.text: A neural network classifier model combined with wavelet transform (DWT) and dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT) can automatically detect and classify ventricular and supraventricular cardiac arrhythmias with high accuracy.

The combination of discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT) enables effective feature extraction from ECG signals, including QRS complex detection and segmentation of P, Q, R, S, and T waves.
Noise in ECG signals can be effectively reduced using adaptive filtering and wavelet-based soft thresholding techniques, improving the accuracy of subsequent feature extraction and classification.
The dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT) outperforms the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) in pattern recognition tasks due to its lower energy discrepancy in wavelet coefficients.

The proposed method achieves high accuracy in classifying cardiac arrhythmias by training a neural network with features extracted from ECG signals using DWT and DTCWT, validated on multiple datasets including MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm Database, Supraventricular Arrhythmia Database, and Malignant Ventricular Arrhythmia Database.

similar_papers.title: Attention-Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network for Inter-patient Classification of Premature Ventricular Contraction from ECG
similar_papers.abstract: Premature ventricular contraction (PVC) is a common type of cardiac arrhythmia characterized by an early and irregular heartbeat originating from the ventricles. This study presents a dual-path CNN network (WACNN) designed based on wavelet decomposition and attention mechanisms for detecting PVCs from single-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs). All ECG recordings are firstly resampled to 256 Hz. The R-peak positions detected using the Pan-Tompkins method are firstly used to extract a 256 points fixed-duration as training set A, and then used to extract two complete RR intervals as another training set (B). Subsequently, all segments in training set B are resampled to 512 points, resulting in a rescaled training set C. Set B and set C are fed into the model through two separate paths for training. The ratio of the original segment length in B to 512 is considered as a critical infection feature (heart rate feature) for PVC detection in the model. The proposed model is trained on 11 recordings from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database (MITAD) and validated on another 11 recordings, excluding pacemaker data. Testing is conducted on the remaining 22 recordings. On the test dataset, the model achieved a precision of 95.41%, recall of 98.72%, F1 score of 97.04%, and overall accuracy of 99.63%, outperforming most existing methods.

claims.text: A dual-path convolutional neural network incorporating wavelet decomposition and attention mechanisms effectively detects premature ventricular contractions from single-lead electrocardiograms by utilizing both morphological characteristics of individual heartbeats and features of surrounding heartbeats.

The preprocessing method includes resampling ECG recordings to 256 Hz, detecting R-peak positions using the Pan-Tompkins method, extracting fixed-duration segments and complete RR intervals, and rescaling segments to 512 points, with the RR ratio used as a critical feature for premature ventricular contraction detection.

The dual-path architecture combines features extracted from fixed-duration segments and wavelet-transformed RR intervals, enhanced by Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks for channel attention, to produce a robust feature representation for premature ventricular contraction classification.

The proposed model leverages a focal loss function to address class imbalance in premature ventricular contraction detection and employs early stopping to optimize training epochs based on validation loss.

The innovative heartbeat segmentation method incorporates heart rate recalibration and compensatory pause characteristics, improving the accuracy of premature ventricular contraction detection compared to traditional fixed-duration segmentation approaches.

similar_papers.title: Automatic Detection of Atrial Fibrillation Based on Continuous Wavelet Transform and 2D Convolutional Neural Networks
similar_papers.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmias causing morbidity and mortality. AF may appear as episodes of very short (i.e., proximal AF) or sustained duration (i.e., persistent AF), either form of which causes irregular ventricular excitations that affect the global function of the heart. It is an unmet challenge for early and automatic detection of AF, limiting efficient treatment strategies for AF. In this study, we developed a new method based on continuous wavelet transform and 2D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to detect AF episodes. The proposed method analyzed the time-frequency features of the electrocardiogram (ECG), thus being different to conventional AF detecting methods that implement isolating atrial or ventricular activities. Then a 2D CNN was trained to improve AF detection performance. The MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation Database was used for evaluating the algorithm. The efficacy of the proposed method was compared with those of some existing methods, most of which implemented the same dataset. The newly developed algorithm using CNNs achieved 99.41, 98.91, 99.39, and 99.23% for the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and overall accuracy (ACC) respectively. As the proposed algorithm targets the time-frequency feature of ECG signals rather than isolated atrial or ventricular activity, it has the ability to detect AF episodes for using just five beats, suggesting practical applications in the future.

claims.text: A method combining continuous wavelet transform and 2D convolutional neural networks can automatically detect atrial fibrillation episodes by analyzing time-frequency features of electrocardiogram signals without isolating atrial or ventricular activities.
The proposed algorithm can detect atrial fibrillation episodes using only five beats of electrocardiogram data, demonstrating potential for practical clinical applications.

Continuous wavelet transform transforms one-dimensional electrocardiogram signals into two-dimensional time-frequency patterns, enabling convolutional neural networks to automatically extract spatio-temporal features for atrial fibrillation classification.

The developed algorithm achieves superior sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and overall accuracy compared to existing methods for atrial fibrillation detection using the MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation Database.

The proposed convolutional neural network architecture eliminates the need for manual feature extraction and achieves high performance in atrial fibrillation classification by leveraging automatically extracted features from time-frequency representations of electrocardiogram signals.

similar_papers.title: CNN Based ECG Dual Heart Beat Arrhythmia Detection
similar_papers.abstract:
Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals are crucial in the
process of cardiac diagnosis as well as ongoing monitoring of
health. However, achieving best performance is difficult due
to factors such as large variations between patients,
imbalanced heartbeat classes, and very subtle differences
between certain abnormal beats. Although convolutional
neural networks (CNNs) have become popular for ECG
classification because of their strong ability to learn features,
models based on singlebeat ECG representations often fail to
capture important beattobeat information.To address these
limitations, this work proposes a dualheartbeat CNNbased
framework for ECG arrhythmia classification. Instead of
analyzing each heartbeat independently, the method
combines neighbouring heartbeats to capture both waveform
characteristics and temporal relationships between beats.
ECG signals are segmented around detected Rpeaks, and
adjacent beats are transformed into twodimensional coupling
matrices that serve as inputs to the CNN. In addition, a
systematic training beat selection strategy is applied to
improve learning for less frequent arrhythmia types.The
proposed framework is evaluated using the MITBIH
Arrhythmia Database following AAMIrecommended
evaluation protocols. Performance is assessed using standard
metrics such as sensitivity, precision, and overall accuracy.
Experimental results show that the dualheartbeat CNN
approach outperforms conventional single-beat CNN models,
particularly in detecting supraventricular ectopic beats,
where sensitivity improves by approximately 5%to12% while
maintaining consistent performance for other heartbeat
classes .The suggested approach offers an entirely automatic
and stable ECG analysis framework that does not require
manual feature eliciting or professional assistance.

claims.text: A dual-heartbeat convolutional neural network (CNN) framework for ECG arrhythmia classification captures both morphological and temporal relationships between successive heartbeats by transforming adjacent beats into two-dimensional coupling matrices.

The dual-heartbeat CNN approach improves sensitivity in detecting rare arrhythmias, such as supraventricular ectopic beats, by incorporating a systematic training beat selection strategy to address class imbalance.
The proposed framework eliminates the need for manual feature extraction by leveraging end-to-end learning with CNNs, enabling fully automated and robust ECG arrhythmia classification.

The dual-heartbeat representation enhances the detection of rhythm-dependent arrhythmias by integrating beat-to-beat temporal information with morphological features in a two-dimensional input format.

Evaluation on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database using AAMI-recommended protocols demonstrates that the dual-heartbeat CNN framework outperforms single-beat models in classifying arrhythmias, particularly for supraventricular ectopic beats.

similar_papers.title: SAR ship target detection method based on CNN structure with wavelet and attention mechanism
similar_papers.abstract: Ship target detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images is an important application field. Due to the existence of sea clutter, especially the SAR imaging in huge wave area, SAR images contain a lot of complex noise, which brings great challenges to the effective detection of ship targets in SAR images. Although the deep semantic segmentation network has been widely used in the detection of ship targets in recent years, the global information of the image cannot be fully utilized. To solve this problem, a new convolutional neural network (CNN) method based on wavelet and attention mechanism was proposed in this paper, called the WA-CNN algorithm. The new method uses the U-Net structure to construct the network, which not only effectively reduces the depth of the network structure, but also significantly improves the complexity of the network. The basic network of WA-CNN algorithm consists of encoder and decoder. Dual tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT) is introduced into the pooling layer of the encoder to smooth the speckle noise in SAR images, which is beneficial to preserve the contour structure and detail information of the target in the feature image. The attention mechanism theory is added into the decoder to obtain the global information of the ship target. Two public SAR image datasets were used to verify the proposed method, and good experimental results were obtained. This shows that the method proposed in this article is effective and feasible.

claims.text: The WA-CNN algorithm, based on a U-Net structure, incorporates dual-tree complex wavelet transform in the encoder to reduce speckle noise and preserve structural features in SAR images, and introduces an attention mechanism in the decoder to enhance global feature extraction and improve ship target detection.

The WA-CNN algorithm significantly reduces network complexity and parameter count compared to other methods like FCN, U-Net, and DeepLabv3+, while achieving superior ship detection performance in SAR images.

The wavelet pooling layer in the WA-CNN algorithm effectively suppresses speckle noise in SAR images by leveraging low-frequency sub-images from dual-tree complex wavelet transform, preserving detailed structural features such as edges and corners.

The attention mechanism in the WA-CNN algorithm improves the utilization of middle-layer features and enhances the extraction of global information, leading to more accurate ship target detection in SAR images.

Experimental results on SSDD and SAR-SHIP-SET datasets demonstrate that the WA-CNN algorithm outperforms FCN, U-Net, and DeepLabv3+ in terms of sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and AUC for ship target detection in SAR images.

similar_papers.title: Electrocardiogram Based Arrhythmia Classification Using Long Short-Term Memory with Luong Attention Mechanism
similar_papers.abstract: : The Electrocardiogram (ECG) serves as a crucial indicator of diverse cardiac conditions, emphasizing the importance of precise signal classification for automated arrhythmia detection. ECG is an efficient tool for the diagnosis and detection of arrhythmia. Detecting arrhythmias in extended ECG segments can result in episodes being overlooked. However, since ECG transmits a massive amount of information, it becomes very complex and challenging to extract the relevant information from visual analysis. To overcome this problem, this research proposes Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with Luong Attention Mechanism approach for the classification of arrhythmia from ECG into 5 classes. When LSTM is combined with Luong attention, they can learn which parts of the ECG signal are crucial at each time step, and effectively capturing both short-term and long-term dependencies. For evaluating the performance of the proposed method, the data is collected from a benchmark dataset called the MIT-BIH dataset. After the collection of the dataset, the pre-processing is done using Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) to reduce the low and high-frequency noise. After that, the pre-processed data is forwarded to the feature extraction process to extract the relevant features by using the statistical (Skewness, Kurtosis, Moment, etc.) and time-frequency domain features. Finally, the LSTM is used to classify the arrhythmia classes. From this analysis, the proposed LSTM with Luong Attention Mechanism achieved better results in overall metrics. The proposed method achieves the accuracy of 99.75% which is comparatively higher than the existing approaches like Deep Residual Convolutional Neural Network (DRCNN) and Depth wise Separable CNN with Focal Loss (DSC-FL-CNN).

claims.text: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) combined with the Luong Attention Mechanism effectively classifies arrhythmia from electrocardiogram signals into five classes by capturing both short-term and long-term dependencies and selectively attending to relevant signal parts.

Pre-processing of electrocardiogram signals using Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) removes baseline wandering and reduces low and high-frequency noise, enhancing the accuracy of arrhythmia classification.
Statistical and time-frequency domain features extracted from electrocardiogram signals improve dimensionality reduction and data compaction, enabling efficient classification of arrhythmia.

The Luong Attention Mechanism enhances the performance of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models by applying attention weights to significant parts of input sequences, improving the interpretability and accuracy of arrhythmia classification.

The proposed method achieves higher accuracy in arrhythmia classification compared to existing approaches such as Deep Residual Convolutional Neural Network (DRCNN) and Depth-wise Separable CNN with Focal Loss (DSC-FL-CNN) using the MIT-BIH dataset.

similar_papers.title: Hybird RNN based feature extraction for early prediction of CVDs using ECG Signals for type 2 diabetic patients
similar_papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus patients are at an increased risk of cardiovascular illness, and cardiovascular complications are the primary cause of morbidity. Diabetes is linked to both morbidity and mortality. Type-2 Diabetes causes a prothrombotic state that leads to acute coronary syndromes by causing endothelial damage and lowering antiaggregant factors like nitric oxide and prostacyclin, as well as increasing thrombotic substances like fibrinogen and factor VII, and suppressing fibrinolysis with factors like plasminogen activator inhibitors. The accurate identification and diagnosis of CVD (Cardio Vascular Disease) is dependent on the correct detection of the ECG signal from the heart. The ECG signal is extremely important in the early detection of cardiac problems. The ECG signal of diabetic individuals offers vital information about the heart and is one of the most important diagnostic tools used by doctors to identify cardiovascular disorders. The time gap between two consecutive QRS complexes appearing contiguous in an ECG is known as heart rate.  The most appealing feature is that HRV (Heart Rate Variability) measurement is non-invasive and repeatable. A number of machine learning techniques have been proposed for the non-invasive automated identification of diabetes. This paper discusses innovative methods for analyzing electrocardiogram (ECG) signals in order to extract important diagnostic information. The ECG signal is first treated using a dual tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT-SG) with threshold method. Subsequently, the features are extracted from detailed coefficients of DTCWT-SG filter, Eigen vectors by minimum normalization method and Rajan Transform. Main key features are extracted using these three methods. These features are classified and analyzed by different machine learning classifiers. The proposed approach was tested on DICARDIA, MIT-BIH and Physionet database and the performance analysis shows that the hybrid Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) (LSTM+GRU Gated Recurrent Units) achieves better prediction of 98.8% compared to state of art techniques.

claims.text: A hybrid recurrent neural network model combining long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent units (GRU) with an Adaboost classifier achieves improved classification accuracy for early prediction of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) in type-2 diabetic patients using electrocardiogram (ECG) signals.

A novel dual tree complex wavelet transform with a Savitzky-Golay filter (DTCWT-SG) effectively removes noise from ECG signals, including baseline wander, electromyographical noise, and powerline interference, enabling accurate feature extraction for CVD diagnosis.

Key diagnostic features such as R-peak, R-R interval, QRS complex, and PR and ST segments can be extracted from ECG signals using a combination of DTCWT-SG filtering, eigen vector-based minimum normalization, and Rajan transform methods.

The proposed method categorizes ECG signals of type-2 diabetic patients into three classes—normal, early stage, and abnormal—based on extracted features and hybrid RNN classification, providing a more granular diagnosis compared to traditional binary classification methods.

The hybrid RNN model with Adaboost classifier demonstrates superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, achieving a classification accuracy of 98.8%, precision of 97.8%, and recall of 98.6% on DICARDIA, MIT-BIH, and Physionet ECG databases.

anchor_claims.text: Dual Tree Wavelet Transform provides enhanced feature extraction capabilities for ECG signal analysis, offering advantages such as shift invariance and directional selectivity, which improve the classification of cardiac arrhythmias.
Convolutional Neural Networks effectively classify ECG signals into different arrhythmia categories, leveraging extracted features from Dual Tree Wavelet Transform for improved diagnostic accuracy.

The combination of Dual Tree Wavelet Transform and Convolutional Neural Networks demonstrates high generalizability and reduces misdiagnosis in computer-aided detection of critical and non-critical cardiac arrhythmias.

Dual Tree Wavelet Transform generates complex-valued subbands that enhance signal representation in both time and frequency domains, facilitating the identification of cardiac abnormalities such as Atrial Fibrillation, Myocardial Infarction, and Bundle Branch Block.

The Physionet database provides high-quality ECG signals that, when processed using Dual Tree Wavelet Transform and classified with Convolutional Neural Networks, enable accurate detection of arrhythmias and cardiovascular diseases.

**Summary: Cardiac Arrhythmia Detection Using Dual-Tree Wavelet Transform and Convolutional Neural Network**

The integration of the dual-tree wavelet transform (DTWT) with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) represents a powerful approach for the automatic detection and classification of cardiac arrhythmias from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. DTWT excels in cardiac signal analysis by providing enhanced feature extraction through its dual (real and complex) decompositions, which offer improved shift invariance and directional selectivity compared to single-tree transforms like the discrete wavelet transform (DWT). This capability effectively captures both time and frequency domain characteristics of ECG signals, facilitating the identification of key features such as the QRS complex, P, Q, R, S, and T wave segments, as well as distinguishing between various arrhythmias including atrial fibrillation, myocardial infarction, bundle branch block, and ventricular ectopics.

The extracted wavelet features serve as robust input to CNNs, which are adept at learning hierarchical patterns in complex medical data. CNN architectures, whether conventional or enhanced with attention mechanisms or beat-to-beat relationships (e.g., dual-heartbeat CNNs), can classify arrhythmias with high sensitivity and specificity across multiple datasets, including the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database and others. By leveraging DTWT preprocessing (including denoising using techniques such as Savitzky-Golay filtering), noise such as baseline wander and powerline interference is reduced, improving signal quality for subsequent analysis.

Compared to traditional methods relying solely on hand-crafted features or simple classifiers, the DTWT–CNN framework achieves state-of-the-art classification performance with high accuracy, generalizability, and reduced misdiagnosis rates. Moreover, advanced hybrid techniques—such as integrating optimization algorithms like the Horse Herd Optimization Algorithm, or combining wavelet transformations with 1D CNNs and attention modules—further enhance detection robustness, especially in scenarios with class imbalance or noisy signals.

In summary, the combination of dual-tree wavelet transform for advanced feature extraction and CNNs for deep learning classification forms a highly effective and computationally efficient pipeline for automated cardiac arrhythmia detection. This approach enables early diagnosis, clinical decision support, and the potential for point-of-care implementation, offering a significant advancement in medical signal processing and arrhythmia monitoring.

**Cardiac Arrhythmia Detection using Dual-Tree Wavelet Transform and Convolutional Neural Network**

Cardiac arrhythmia detection is a critical task in cardiovascular disease diagnosis. Recent advances in signal processing and deep learning have enabled the development of accurate and efficient detection methods. The combination of dual-tree wavelet transform (DTWT) and convolutional neural network (CNN) has shown promising results in detecting cardiac arrhythmias.

**Dual-Tree Wavelet Transform:**

DTWT is a shift-invariant and directional-selective wavelet transform that provides enhanced feature extraction capabilities for ECG signal analysis. It generates complex-valued subbands that enhance signal representation in both time and frequency domains, facilitating the identification of cardiac abnormalities such as atrial fibrillation, myocardial infarction, and bundle branch block.

**Convolutional Neural Network:**

CNN is a powerful deep learning architecture that can learn complex patterns in ECG signals. When combined with DTWT, CNN can effectively classify ECG signals into different arrhythmia categories, leveraging extracted features for improved diagnostic accuracy.

**Key Advantages:**

1.  **Shift Invariance:** DTWT provides shift-invariant feature extraction, which is essential for cardiac arrhythmia detection, where subtle changes in signal morphology can indicate arrhythmias.
2.  **Directional Selectivity:** DTWT's directional selectivity enables the extraction of features from different orientations, enhancing the detection of cardiac abnormalities.
3.  **Robustness to Noise:** DTWT can effectively reduce noise in ECG signals, enabling accurate feature extraction and classification.
4.  **High Accuracy:** The combination of DTWT and CNN has achieved high accuracy in detecting cardiac arrhythmias, outperforming traditional methods.

**Applications:**

1.  **Clinical Diagnosis:** The proposed method can be used for clinical diagnosis of cardiac arrhythmias, enabling accurate and timely detection.
2.  **Remote Monitoring:** The method can be applied to remote monitoring systems, enabling continuous monitoring of patients with cardiac arrhythmias.

Summary: Cardiac Arrhythmia Detection Using Dual-Tree Wavelet Transform and Convolutional Neural Networks

Cardiac arrhythmia detection from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals can be enhanced by combining the Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Transform (DTCWT/DTWT) with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). This hybrid approach exploits the complementary strengths of wavelet-based signal representation and deep-learning-based classification to identify abnormal cardiac patterns accurately and automatically.

Dual-Tree Wavelet Transform for ECG Processing

ECG signals are nonstationary and can be affected by baseline wander, power-line interference, muscle artifacts, and other forms of noise. Dual-tree wavelet transforms provide a multiresolution time-frequency representation that is particularly suitable for analyzing such signals. Compared with the conventional Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), DTCWT provides desirable properties including approximate shift invariance, improved frequency selectivity, and complex-valued wavelet coefficients.

These characteristics can improve the representation of diagnostically important ECG morphology, including:

P, Q, R, S, and T waves
QRS complexes
R-peak locations and R-R intervals
PR and ST segments
Fine morphological variations associated with abnormal cardiac activity

Wavelet-based preprocessing can also suppress noise and baseline variations while retaining clinically informative structures. The resulting coefficients or derived features provide CNNs with a richer representation of the ECG in the time-frequency domain.

CNN-Based Arrhythmia Classification

CNNs complement DTCWT by automatically learning discriminative patterns from wavelet-derived ECG representations. Depending on how the ECG is represented, 1D CNNs can process sequences of ECG or wavelet coefficients directly, while 2D CNNs can analyze time-frequency representations as image-like inputs.

The studies in the supplied context collectively indicate that CNN architectures can reduce dependence on manually engineered diagnostic features. They learn hierarchical representations that distinguish normal cardiac activity from abnormalities such as:

Atrial fibrillation
Supraventricular ectopic beats
Ventricular ectopic beats
Premature ventricular contractions
Bundle branch block
Myocardial infarction-related ECG abnormalities

Temporal context can further improve classification. For example, architectures operating on adjacent heartbeats can combine beat morphology with beat-to-beat rhythm information, which is particularly useful for arrhythmias that cannot be reliably characterized from a single heartbeat.

Why DTCWT and CNNs Are Complementary

A typical hybrid framework can be represented as:

Raw ECG → Noise suppression/normalization → Heartbeat segmentation → DTCWT decomposition → Time-frequency feature representation → CNN feature learning → Arrhythmia classification

DTCWT acts as a signal-aware front end, decomposing ECG signals into informative multiscale components. The CNN then acts as a data-driven feature learner and classifier, identifying complex relationships within those components.

This combination can offer several advantages:

Improved robustness to signal shifts and noise through DTCWT-based representation.
Preservation of transient ECG morphology across multiple frequency scales.
Automatic extraction of discriminative features using CNNs.
Reduced reliance on handcrafted ECG descriptors.
Better discrimination of morphologically similar heartbeat classes.
Potentially improved generalizability and diagnostic reliability, particularly when evaluated using patient-independent protocols.
Supporting Developments

The broader literature represented in the supplied material reinforces this basic architecture. Continuous Wavelet Transform combined with 2D CNNs has been applied to atrial-fibrillation detection, while Wavelet Scattering Transform coupled with 1D CNNs has been used for inter-patient heartbeat classification. Other approaches introduce attention mechanisms, LSTM/GRU networks, focal loss, SMOTE, and optimization algorithms to improve temporal modeling, class-imbalance handling, or CNN hyperparameter selection.

These studies collectively suggest that the principal value of wavelet-CNN systems comes from combining an effective time-frequency representation of ECG physiology with the automatic nonlinear pattern-recognition capability of deep neural networks.

Conclusion

Overall, Dual-Tree Wavelet Transform combined with Convolutional Neural Networks provides a promising framework for automated cardiac arrhythmia detection. DTCWT enhances ECG representation through multiresolution, approximately shift-invariant time-frequency analysis, while CNNs automatically learn features capable of differentiating normal and abnormal cardiac patterns. Evidence across the provided studies also supports wavelet-based preprocessing as a useful complement to deep learning, especially for preserving ECG morphology, reducing noise, and improving discrimination among arrhythmia classes.

For clinical translation, however, high classification accuracy alone is insufficient. Robust evaluation should emphasize inter-patient testing, independent datasets, class-specific sensitivity and specificity, resistance to ECG noise and acquisition variability, and external validation to establish whether improvements observed on benchmark databases translate into reliable real-world arrhythmia detection.

These studies collectively suggest that the principal value of wavelet-CNN systems comes from combining an effective time-frequency representation of ECG physiology with the automatic nonlinear pattern-recognition capability of deep neural networks.

similar_papers.title: Securing medical data by role-based user policy with partially homomorphic encryption in AWS cloud
similar_papers.abstract: Cloud technology provides services for storing and accessing a large amount of data with ease of access and less cost. Sensitive data such as patients' electronic health information should be encrypted before outsourcing into the cloud. Many traditional encryption methods are used for protecting data in the cloud, but unable to perform computation on encrypted data. Homomorphic encryption operates directly on the ciphertext. In this study, a Secure Partially Homomorphic Encryption (SPHE) algorithm is proposed to secure the outsourced data and perform multiplication and division operations on the ciphertext. The access control policy in the cloud environment is more flexible. An attacker can easily collect sensitive data by abusing the access policy of another user. Therefore, the database privacy is compromised. Creating a role hierarchy and managing the session is difficult in the cloud environment. The above issues motivate us to develop a model which is the integration of the proposed scheme SPHE with role-based user policy. The model is implemented in Eclipse IDE (Integrated Development Environment) and AWS (Amazon Web Service) Toolkit for Eclipse and deployed in Amazon Elastic Beanstalk (EB) environment. This model is particularly used for securing the patient e-health details and performing computation on outsourced data. The patient details are encrypted by the algorithm SPHE and uploaded in AWS S3 (Simple Storage Service) bucket. The users are created by AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) service and the access level policy is defined based on user roles in EB environment. The proposed model performance is studied by comparing with other partially homomorphic methods Elgamal, Pailler, and Benaloh. This model achieves data integrity and data confidentiality using the role-based user policy with SPHE.

claims.text: A Secure Partially Homomorphic Encryption (SPHE) algorithm is developed to secure outsourced medical data and enable multiplication and division operations directly on ciphertext.

The SPHE algorithm integrates with a role-based user policy in the AWS cloud environment to ensure data confidentiality and integrity by defining access levels for different user roles such as administrators, evaluators, and end-users.

The SPHE algorithm uses probabilistic encryption with a randomly generated prime number and supports modular arithmetic operations, making it semantically secure and resistant to plaintext guessing attacks.

The proposed SPHE-based model demonstrates better performance in encryption, decryption, and ciphertext storage compared to other partially homomorphic encryption methods such as Elgamal, Paillier, and Benaloh.
The SPHE-based model is implemented and deployed using Amazon Elastic Beanstalk and Amazon S3, with client-side encryption ensuring that the cloud provider cannot access the data or keys.

similar_papers.title: Hierarchical Role-Based Access Control with Homomorphic Encryption for Database as a Service
similar_papers.abstract: Database as a service provides services for accessing and managing customers data which provides ease of access, and the cost is less for these services. There is a possibility that the DBaaS service provider may not be trusted, and data may be stored on untrusted server. The access control mechanism can restrict users from unauthorized access, but in cloud environment access control policies are more flexible. However, an attacker can gather sensitive information for a malicious purpose by abusing the privileges as another user and so database security is compromised. The other problems associated with the DBaaS are to manage role hierarchy and secure session management for query transaction in the database. In this paper, a role-based access control for the multitenant database with role hierarchy is proposed. The query is granted with least access privileges, and a session key is used for session management. The proposed work protects data from privilege escalation and SQL injection. It uses the partial homomorphic encryption (Paillier Encryption) for the encrypting the sensitive data. If a query is to perform any operation on sensitive data, then extra permissions are required for accessing sensitive data. Data confidentiality and integrity are achieved using the role-based access control with partial homomorphic encryption.

claims.text: A role-based access control mechanism with role hierarchy and session management is proposed for multi-tenant databases in Database-as-a-Service (DBaaS) environments to enhance data confidentiality and integrity.

The proposed approach uses partial homomorphic encryption (Paillier encryption) to secure sensitive data during query execution and storage, providing protection against cryptographic attacks such as chosen-plaintext attacks (IND-CPA) and adaptive chosen-ciphertext attacks (IND-CCA2).

The access control mechanism includes features such as user authentication with session key generation using Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA-2), group authentication with group keys, and role activation and deactivation to enforce least privilege and prevent privilege escalation.
The proposed system manages role hierarchy using a Nested Set model, which requires a single entry for each role and ensures efficient role activation and deactivation for secure query execution.

The system protects against SQL injection attacks by requiring role activation for query execution and ensures that sensitive data access requires additional permissions, with sensitive data encrypted using a private key and decrypted using a public key.

similar_papers.title: An Efficient Multi-User Groupwise Integrity CP-ABE(GI-CPABE) for Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Cloud Blockchain Transactions
similar_papers.abstract: As the size of medical data grows exponentially, safeguarding Electronic Health Records (EHR) via cloud blockchain transactions becomes increasingly critical. This paper presents the Multi-User Groupwise Integrity Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Encryption (GI-CPABE), an efficient framework designed to ensure robust data security. By implementing an Improved Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Encryption (ICP-ABE), the GI-CPABE framework is designed to be compatible with both homogeneous and heterogeneous cloud environments, providing secure access that is role-specific and reliable. A distinctive feature of this framework is its role-based access control mechanism, which efficiently assigns user access rights and roles based on multi-user group attributes, considered as integrity measures. An experimental setup was established on a real-time cloud server, simulating a cloud based EHR system. Test data, mimicking real-world EHRs, was generated and subjected to encryption and decryption processes, evaluating the time efficiency of these operations. The proposed GI-CPABE framework demonstrated optimized storage utilization by calculating the overhead of encrypted data, ensuring data integrity through defined attribute-based policies, and enabling secure, controlled access to medical data. Furthermore, a comparative analysis was conducted to ascertain the effectiveness of the proposed framework against existing models. The implementation of access control mechanisms exhibited robust enforcement of access controls tailored to different user roles such as healthcare providers, patients, and administrators.

The proposed framework integrates blockchain technology with cryptographic hashing methods, such as SHA256, to enhance the security and integrity of electronic health records during storage and access.
The GI-CPABE framework supports secure multi-user communication by generating unique secret keys for users based on their roles and attributes, enabling controlled access to encrypted medical data.

The experimental results demonstrate that the GI-CPABE framework outperforms traditional encryption models in terms of access control efficiency, transaction throughput, and runtime performance for encryption and decryption processes in cloud-based medical applications.

similar_papers.title: Secure Phrase Search for Intelligent Processing of Encrypted Data in Cloud-Based IoT
similar_papers.abstract: Phrase search allows retrieval of documents containing an exact phrase, which plays an important role in many machine learning applications for cloud-based Internet of Things (IoT), such as intelligent medical data analytics. In order to protect sensitive information from being leaked by service providers, documents (e.g., clinic records) are usually encrypted by data owners before being outsourced to the cloud. This, however, makes the search operation an extremely challenging task. Existing searchable encryption schemes for multikeyword search operations fail to perform phrase search, as they are unable to determine the location relationship of multiple keywords in a queried phrase over encrypted data on the cloud server side. In this paper, we propose P3, an efficient privacy-preserving phrase search scheme for intelligent encrypted data processing in cloud-based IoT. Our scheme exploits the homomorphic encryption and bilinear map to determine the location relationship of multiple queried keywords over encrypted data. It also utilizes a probabilistic trapdoor generation algorithm to protect users’ search patterns. Thorough security analysis demonstrates the security guarantees achieved by P3. We implement a prototype and conduct extensive experiments on real-world datasets. The evaluation results show that compared with existing multikeyword search schemes, P3 can greatly improve the search accuracy with moderate overheads.

claims.text: A privacy-preserving phrase search scheme, P3, enables efficient phrase search over encrypted data in cloud-based IoT by utilizing homomorphic encryption and bilinear maps to determine the positional relationship of queried keywords without relying on a trusted third party.
The P3 scheme employs a probabilistic trapdoor generation algorithm to protect user search patterns and ensures trapdoor unlinkability by incorporating dummy keywords and secure kNN techniques.

The P3 scheme achieves higher search accuracy compared to multi-keyword conjunctive search schemes by accurately identifying documents containing exact phrases while maintaining moderate computational and communication overheads.

The P3 scheme provides security guarantees under both known ciphertext and known background models by ensuring index privacy and trapdoor unlinkability through probabilistic encryption and secure keyword representation.

The P3 scheme supports efficient single-interaction phrase search over encrypted data, eliminating the need for multiple rounds of client-server interaction and reducing communication overheads compared to existing phrase search solutions.

similar_papers.title: A New Authentication and Homomorphic Encryption as a Service Model for Preserving Privacy in Clouds
similar_papers.abstract: The security as a Service (SECaaS) is a new model which provides security solution to users through Cloud Computing. The maturity of Cloud Computing services makes possible the use of the SECaaS model. This new model offers huge benefits to users, such as Authentication as a Service (AaaS) and Encryption as a Service (ENCaaS). So, it can offer more security features, since it uses the resources of Clouds and it’s connected to the different security policy databases. While SECaaS offers to cloud users and companies a multitude of security services, it still remains very limited and several aspects of security are not covered by this model, especially the part concerning the privacy. In addition, SECaaS is a new model that is not yet correctly deployed and it is not sufficiently solicited by companies. On the other side, Homomorphic encryption is considered as a good solution to ensure the privacy for users using the cloud services because it permits to make calculation on cipher text and data without decrypting them, but this solution suffer from many limitations such as the key size, the high latency and some serious performance problems. The main idea of this paper it’s to propose a new security model to preserving user’s privacy using homomorphic encryption while bypassing its limitations. So, This paper proposes a framework for Authentication and Homomorphic Encryption (A-HEaaS) based on security as a Service model which permits a secure access to the Cloud servers and the use of homomorphic encryption for calculations on encrypted data. The paper describes the design of our model and gives an implementation of our framework on medical Data.

similar_papers.title: Hybrid high performance intelligent computing approach of CACNN and RNN for skin cancer image grading
similar_papers.abstract: Skin cancer is defined as unregulated cell proliferation due to irreversible DNA damage. Melanoma is one kind of skin cancer generated by melanocytes, which could result in serious health issues. Early detection of this skin cancer based on image processing assist therapists in its treatment. Computational pathology has the unique capability of spatially dissecting specific interfaces on digitized histology images. The main objective of this research is to classify skin cancer using a deep learning model. This work proposes a hybrid context-aware convolutional neural network with recurrent neural network (CA-CNN-RNN) based on skin cancer histology images. This model encodes the local representation of the histological images into high-dimensional features and hence aggregates the features by considering their spatial configuration for performing final classification. The dataset for this work is made up of H&E-stained images from the database of The Cancer Genome Atlas. Using the hybrid CA-CNN-RNN model, the experiment on histological image of melanoma disease was performed and validated with several classification models like DarkNet-53, VGG-19, ResNet50, and Inception. The data set is utilized to evaluate the model in order to provide results, which are analyzed using parameters like as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The experimental analysis reveals that the CA-CNN-RNN performed better with the DarkNet-53 model. The proposed model achieved 97.14 accuracy, 96.49 precision, 98.21 recall, and 96.50 f-score.

Among the tested classifiers, the DarkNet-53 model achieved the best performance across all evaluation parameters, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F-score, for melanoma skin cancer grading using the CA-CNN-RNN model.
The proposed CA-CNN-RNN model is robust and can be adapted for different cancer grading tasks by utilizing appropriate datasets and advanced deep learning models.

similar_papers.title: RETRACTED: A N-gram based approach to auto-extracting topics from research articles
similar_papers.abstract: A lot of manual work goes into identifying a topic for an article. With a large volume of articles, the manual process can be exhausting. Our approach aims to address this issue by automatically extracting topics from the text of large numbers of articles. This approach takes into account the efficiency of the process. Based on existing N-gram analysis, our research examines how often certain words appear in documents in order to support automatic topic extraction. In order to improve efficiency, we apply custom filtering standards to our research. Additionally, delete as many noncritical or irrelevant phrases as possible. In this way, we can ensure we are selecting unique keyphrases for each article, which capture its core idea1. For our research, we chose to center on the autonomous vehicle domain, since the research is relevant to our daily lives. We have to convert the PDF versions of most of the research papers into editable types of files such as TXT. This is because most of the research papers are only in PDF format. To test our proposed idea of automating, numerous articles on robotics have been selected. Next, we evaluate our approach by comparing the result with other models.

similar_papers.title: Topic Modelling in Computer Security Discourse: a Case Study of Whitepaper Publications and News Feeds
similar_papers.abstract: Up-to-date information plays a crucial role in modern linguistic research. For this reason,computational linguistic methods, including those aided with analytical and machine-learning tools, are attracting growing attention. Some of their applications in cognitive-discursive linguistics are keyword extraction, topic modelling, and content analysis. Text-mining tools facilitate time-consuming linguistic work andadd to the results’ reliability and greater statistical precision by processing a significantly larger data volume.Most studies, however, have overlooked interference of socially significant but context-irrelevant (e.g. political) information into a specialized discourse by focusing mainly on one data format. The current study,aimed at topic modelling, has been carried out on the computer security discourse. We have implemented theproject on the KNIME analytical platform. The model enables comparison between topics extracted frompublished articles and date-specific RSS news feeds. The study provides important insights into infodemiology and political incidental news exposure occurring in computer-security-oriented RSS feeds on theKaspersky website but untraceable in the papers published on the same website in a PDF format. The resultsreported here provide further evidence for the need to consider the hypercontext of professional communication and employ real-time data in solving similar problems within cognitive-discursive linguistics.Our contribution to the development of cognitive-discursive linguistics is the method for comparingtopics within one discourse, taking into account near-real-time data. For computational linguistics, the significance of our work lies in describing a new application of the topic extraction workflow freely available onthe KNIME hub.

similar_papers.title: Editorial: Mining Scientific Papers, Volume II: Knowledge Discovery and Data Exploitation
similar_papers.abstract: The Research Topic on “Knowledge Discovery and Data Exploitation” aims at promoting interdisciplinary research in computational linguistics and in Natural Language Processing (NLP) applied to the fields of Bibliometrics, Scientometrics, and Information Retrieval. It is a follow-up of our previous Research Topic: “Mining Scientific Papers: NLP-enhanced Bibliometrics” (Atanassova et al., 2019). The processing of scientific texts, which includes the analysis of citation contexts but also the task of information extraction from scientific papers for various applications, has been the object of intensive research during the last decade. This has become possible thanks to two factors. The first one is the growing availability of scientific papers in full text and in machine-readable formats together with the rise of the Open Access publishing of papers on online platforms such as ArXiv, Semantic Scholar, CiteSeer, or PLOS. The second factor is the relative maturity of open source tools and libraries for natural language processing that facilitate text processing (e.g., Spacy, NLTK, Mallet, OpenNLP, CoreNLP, Gate, CiteSpace). As a result, a large number of experiments have been conducted by processing the full text of papers for citation context analysis, but also summarization and recommendation of scientific papers. This Research Topic aims to discuss novel approaches that focus on the processing and exploitation of data extracted from scientific literature. In particular, the possibility to enrich metadata by the full-text processing of papers offers new fields of investigation that are related to the representation of data and the production of knowledge by the aggregation of data from multiple documents. Given the wide range of available techniques, several questions arise in this field: What volume of scientific data should be considered exploitable and allow the production of new knowledge through aggregation? How can knowledge generated from data in scientific articles be represented? What types of data and knowledge can be automatically extracted from scientific articles and how can it be exploited efficiently?

Topic modeling can be used to analyze linguistic patterns in health research abstracts and predict language bias influenced by factors such as time, funding sources, and nation of origin.

A deep attentive neural network trained on abstracts from the Web of Science can effectively classify scientific articles into subject categories, outperforming existing clustering and citation network-based approaches.
The SYMBALS methodology, which combines backward snowballing and active learning, accelerates systematic review processes by improving title and abstract screening efficiency.

similar_papers.title: Editorial: Mining Scientific Papers: NLP-enhanced Bibliometrics
similar_papers.abstract: The Research Topic on “NLP-enhanced Bibliometrics” aims to promote interdisciplinary research in bibliometrics, Natural Language Processing (NLP) and computational linguistics in order to enhance the ways bibliometrics can benefit from large-scale text analytics and sense mining of papers. The objectives of such research are to provide insights into scientific writing and bring new perspectives to the understanding of both the nature of citations and the nature of scientific papers and their internal structures. The possibility to enrichmetadata by the full-text processing of papers offers a new field of investigation, where the major problems arise around the organization and structure of text, the extraction of information and its representation at the level of metadata. Recently, the ever growing availability of datasets and papers in full text and inmachine-readable formats has made possible a change in perspective in the field of bibliometrics. From preprint databases to the Open Access and the Open Science movements, the development of online platforms such as ArXiv, CiteSeer or PLoS and so forth, largely contribute to facilitating the experimentation with datasets of articles, making it possible to perform bibliometric studies not only considering the metadata of papers but also their full text content. The field of NLP offers methodological frameworks and tools for the full text processing of papers that can enlighten bibliometric studies. Some of the open source tools for text processing that have been recently applied to such tasks include NLTK, Mallet, OpenNLP, CoreNLP, Gate, CiteSpace, AllenNLP, and others. Many datasets are now freely available for the community: e.g., PubMed OA, CiteSeerX, JSTOR, ISTEX, Microsoft Academic Graph, ACL anthology, etc. The further developments in this field of study need producing annotated corpora and shared evaluation protocols in order to enable the comparison between different tools andmethods. The development of such resources is an important step to making scientific reproducibility possible.

The development of annotated corpora and shared evaluation protocols is essential for enabling reproducibility and comparison of tools and methods in bibliometric research.
Challenges in bibliometric-enhanced studies include errors from automatic text processing and inconsistencies in author and affiliation identification, requiring manual corrections by domain experts.

similar_papers.title: Enabling Decentralized and Auditable Access Control for IoT through Blockchain and Smart Contracts
similar_papers.abstract: The increase in the interconnection of physical devices and the emergence of the 5 G paradigm foster the generation and distribution of massive amounts of data. The complexity associated with the management of these data requires a suitable access control approach that empowers citizens to control how their data are shared, so potential privacy issues can be mitigated. While well-known access control models are widely used in web and cloud scenarios, the IoT ecosystem needs to address the requirements of lightness, decentralization, and scalability to control the access to data generated by a huge number of heterogeneous devices. This work proposes CapBlock, a design that integrates a capability-based access control model and blockchain technology for a fully distributed evaluation of authorization policies and generation of access credentials using smart contracts. CapBlock is intended to manage the access to information in federated IoT environments where data need to be managed through access control policies defined by different data providers. The feasibility of CapBlock has been successfully evaluated in the scope of the EU research project IoTCrawler, which aims at building a secure search engine for IoT data in large-scale scenarios.

claims.text: Raft is a consensus algorithm designed to manage a replicated log, providing equivalent results to Paxos while being more understandable and offering a better foundation for building practical systems.
Raft improves understandability by decomposing the consensus problem into leader election, log replication, and safety, and by reducing nondeterminism and inconsistencies between servers.
Raft introduces a strong leader model where log entries flow only from the leader to followers, simplifying log management and ensuring consistency.
Raft uses randomized timers for leader election to resolve conflicts quickly and includes a joint consensus mechanism for safe cluster membership changes with overlapping majorities.

A user study demonstrated that Raft is significantly easier for students to learn and understand compared to Paxos, with participants scoring higher on Raft-related quizzes and reporting it as easier to implement and explain.

similar_papers.title: A Decentralized Blockchain-Based Framework for Secure and Trustworthy Data Exchange in IoT-Driven Smart Systems
similar_papers.abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) technologies constitute the foundation of contemporary smart systems, including healthcare monitoring platforms, intelligent campus infrastructures, and urban management solutions. While these systems enable real-time data-driven operations, they remain susceptible to security and trust challenges arising from centralized data control, constrained device capabilities, and limited accountability mechanisms. This paper introduces a decentralized blockchain-based framework aimed at securing IoT data exchange while ensuring integrity, transparency, and controlled access. The proposed framework integrates IoT gateways with a blockchain network in which smart contracts govern device authentication and data access policies. By storing cryptographic proofs rather than raw sensor data on the blockchain, the framework significantly reduces storage overhead while maintaining resistance to tampering. Security evaluation and performance analysis demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively mitigates unauthorized access, data manipulation, and trust-related vulnerabilities, making it suitable for large-scale deployment in future smart environments.
